`begin +4`, `end +8`, and capacity `+0x0C`; command `0x1B` supplies the complete
`[begin,end)` range, so the helper sets `end = begin`. It neither changes the
allocation/capacity member nor zeros the inactive backing records. This is a
script-manager lifetime operation with no observed gameplay-state write.
The hash-bound authoritative `LIBLARY.LIB` routine-40 envelope independently

restored at `0x1D0C`, then seventeen command-`0x1B` rows at

Slot `0x1C` reaches
wrapper `0x0041840B` and vtable slot `+0x64`, resolving to
`0x0041A2A0`. That handler consumes a record plus four individual bytes,
stores the current script coordinate in the manager's internal map under the
evaluated record, and writes the assembled little-endian target as the active

by its evaluated record before swapping into the stored script coordinate.
Together these handlers confirm command `0x1C` as a shared-library routine
registration plus body skip, with structural shape `record + u32-le target`;
it is not a local call.

The authoritative zero-entry-table `LIBLARY.LIB`, SHA-256
`d9aba6eb8dab51fe321e22c868ed0cf38416bba1f0cf2f5d7d719f48e89b8b4d`,

Content Core `0.157.0` advances recursive registered calls to
`kakyu_mes_registered_definition_trace/v5` and adds
`kakyu_mes_registered_definition_continuation/v1`. A dialogue boundary inside

Core call-frame behavior**, **Unresolved native selection semantics**.

Content Core `0.158.0` advances library traces to
`kakyu_mes_library_trace/v7`, Event Runner traces to
`kakyu_mes_event_trace/v62`, and adds
`kakyu_mes_library_continuation/v1`. The library runner now uses the explicit
`skip_bounded_preserve_dialogue` policy: ordinary EXE-bounded character-stream
presentation remains omitted, while the exact message + command-`0x13` +
`02 02 FF 00` trailer remains a user-visible dialogue stop. A stop in a root
or nested indexed routine binds the complete library bytecode hash and routine
index, the exact trailer/resume, command-`0x1D` invocation records, active LIFO
caller frames, and temporary argument/evaluator context. Resume rejects a
changed index/code body, shifted dialogue or caller coordinate, altered call
target, or malformed temporary state before executing more bytecode. This is
a Content Core execution contract; it does not establish new original opcode
meaning. Dialogue inside a registered DEF invoked from a library routine is

Executable audit `kakyu_ai5_mes_exe_audit/v40` narrows the helper boundary

Executable audit v56 first fixed the keyboard and pointer-confirm edges of that

`0x0040A710` asks the DirectInput keyboard interface
through virtual slot `+0x24` for a 256-byte state table and tests the selected

remained outside this bounded input proof. Evidence type: exact original

The same v64 audit binds those slots to the installed modal-control vtable
instead of leaving them as abstract virtual calls. The MES-window constructor
stores table `0x0047D5B0` in its control member at code site `0x00433D9D`.
Its slots are runner `0x0043FD80`, initialize `0x00434A50`, update
`0x00434B90`, confirm `0x00434F50`, mode-gated finalizer `0x00435300`, then
direction wrappers `0x00433CD0`, `0x00433CE0`, `0x00433CF0`, and
`0x00433D00`. The Escape slot points directly at that finalizer. On one
confirmed mode branch the Enter callback also calls the same finalizer through

The four direction wrappers adjust the receiver by `-0x60` and call its parent
virtual slot `+0x24`, forwarding respectively `(0,2)`, `(1,3)`, `(2,4)`, and
`(3,5)`. V57 binds the parent vtable at `0x0047D584` and its slot `+0x24` to
`0x004353A0`. For helper mode 1, that dispatcher asks the selected control at
parent offset `+0x6C` whether it is active through slot `+0x1C`; the installed
mode-1 table `0x00479EC0` resolves that query to `0x00401020`. Only direction
selectors 0 and 1 then reach the same table's slot `+0x0C` function
`0x00401E20`. That function decrements or increments native selection/window
fields at `+0x30/+0x2C`, updates the control, recenters the cursor over the
selected row, and emits the forwarded second value through the host
notification tail. Selectors 2 and 3 do not call this row-navigation function
in mode 1; they remain on the parent cursor/update/notification path.

Both the row-navigation function and parent fallback call `0x00437480`. The
adapter converts the supplied point through the active window's virtual
coordinate-conversion slot and calls imported `USER32.SetCursorPos`; it applies an
additional vertical 40-pixel adjustment in one window state. This proves that
the original keyboard callbacks synchronize the native mouse cursor with the
selection UI instead of maintaining an unrelated keyboard-only cursor. The
modal update at `0x00434B90`
independently samples the screen pointer via
imported `USER32.GetCursorPos`, converts that point through the active window's
virtual slot `+0x48`, and applies a `-40` Y adjustment in window state 2. It
selects the hit-table pointer at control offset `+0x3A4` or `+0x3A0` according
to byte `+0x3DD`, then calls `0x00411400`. That helper walks 10-byte records in
stored order: a word ID followed by inclusive `minX`, `minY`, `maxX`, and
`maxY` words. It returns the first matching ID, or `0xFFFF` at the sentinel/no
match, and the update stores the word at `+0x39C` for the confirm callback.
The confirm callback maps result ID `0x0100` to delta `-1` and result ID
`0x0102` to delta `+1`, then calls helper `0x00435D90`. That helper adds the
delta to the visible-window start at control offset `+0x424`, clamps it to
`0..(count at +0x428 - 1)`, stores it, and refreshes only when it changes. A
separate signed host-delta field reaches the same helper with the same sign
mapping. These two IDs therefore navigate the visible list window; they are
not evidence for selecting a choice record. This closes coordinate sampling,
rectangle hit classification and the two bounded window-navigation effects.

V59 also corrects the hit-table ownership boundary. The modal update receiver
is the control subobject at parent offset `+0x60`, so its pointers `+0x3A0` and
`+0x3A4` are parent offsets `+0x400` and `+0x404`; they are not fields of the
`PARTS.MMO` image object. Constructor `0x00433F45` loads custom `AREA`
resources 142 and 143 and stores their locked payload pointers at those parent
offsets. Resource 142 contains exactly two 10-byte records: ID `0x0000` at
inclusive rectangle `(568,284)..(608,302)` and ID `0x0001` at
`(474,280)..(562,304)`. Resource 143 contains exactly four: ID `0x0100` at
`(480,284)..(520,302)`, ID `0x0101` at `(524,284)..(548,302)`, ID `0x0102`
at `(552,284)..(592,302)`, and ID `0x0103` at
`(598,282)..(616,304)`. Both end with `0xFFFF`. The audit binds the complete
resource payloads by SHA-256 without storing them in documentation. This
proves the only possible hit-ID domains for the two table modes and prevents
MMO pixels from being misclassified as interaction metadata. It still does
not assign cancel/toggle meaning to IDs `0x0000`, `0x0001`, `0x0101`, or
`0x0103`.

V61 retains v60's separation of those modal resources from actual choice rows. The installed
mode-1 `CAdvSelect` vtable points slot `+0x00` to update `0x00401AC0` and slot
`+0x04` to confirm `0x00401C70`. Update samples the converted cursor against a
dynamic table at control offset `+0x10` and stores its current hit word at
`+0x0C`. For a selectable row the hit word's high byte is zero and its low byte
is the ordinal within the visible three-row window. Confirm adds that ordinal
to the window start at `+0x30`, rejects a result outside total count `+0x2C`,
routes routine-40 mode 0 through the host row-mapping slot `+0x4C`, then adds
one before storing the native result. Consequently none of the six embedded
modal `AREA` IDs is a choice row; the one-based row result comes from the
selected control's dynamic table.

V61 closes the pointer-confirm edge without reclassifying those IDs. The
application allocates a `0x2C`-byte key object, stores it at application
offset `+0xF0`, and installs vtable `0x0047AAE4`; slot `+4` is message handler
`0x00437540`. `WM_LBUTTONDOWN` (`0x0201`) captures the game window when needed
and stores `1` at key-object offset `+0x1C`. The exact message jump table maps
`WM_LBUTTONUP` (`0x0202`) to release capture and store `0` at that offset.
Modal update first requires hit-result word `+0x39C` to equal `0`, then treats
that latch as an alternative to Return/Numpad Enter and calls modal confirm
slot `+0x0C`. The confirm callback's ID-0 branch requires its selected-control
gate at `+0x398`, calls the control pointer at modal offset `+0x0C` through
virtual slot `+4`, copies the accepted one-based value from control `+8` to
modal result `+8`, and clears modal running dword `+4`. This is a left-button
down/held latch sampled by update; button-up clears it. `DIK_LCONTROL`
(`0x1D`) and `DIK_RCONTROL` (`0x9D`) also call the same modal confirm callback
using the current hit ID. ID `1` is conditional. When bytes `+0x3DF`,
`+0x3E0`, and `+0x3E1` are all zero, it calls helper `0x00435850` and returns
from the callback without a direct modal-result copy or modal stop. If those
gates do not all pass, the callback falls through to the same selected-control
confirm path. Its final meaning therefore remains deliberately unlabeled
rather than being called cancel or a separate choice row.

V64 also binds the two remaining primary-table branches instead of leaving
their native effects wholly opaque. ID `0x0101` enters the exact callback span
at `0x00434FD4`; it conditionally reads or updates control bytes `+0x3DC` and
`+0x3E0`, calls fixed native helpers `0x004254D0`, `0x0043FFC0`, and
conditionally `0x00435730`, and returns without directly copying modal result
`+8` or clearing modal-running dword `+4`. ID `0x0103` enters at
`0x0043510F`, clears `+0x3DC`, calls `0x00435850` and `0x0043FFC0`, and likewise
returns without a direct result copy or modal stop. These are exact auxiliary
control/presentation-state paths, not selectable rows or direct modal
terminals. Their common helper chain is also exact. `0x00434950` prepares
document region fields; `0x00435730` temporarily sets and restores document
byte `+0xB7A`, clears then sets flag `0x10` at document word `+0x20BC`, and
forwards a rectangle derived from document words
`+0x20C2/+0x20C4/+0x20C6/+0x20C8`. Wrapper `0x0043FFC0` tail-dispatches the
current document embedded object's virtual slot `+0x3C`. These facts do not
prove the visible label or intent of either hit ID, so their user-facing
meanings remain unresolved.

V65 closes the selected-control row-window boundary. The complete original
runtime function `0x00401E20` reads total row count at control `+0x2C`, window
start at `+0x30`, and uses visible ordinals `0..2`; the native choice viewport
therefore contains exactly three rows. Up at ordinal zero decrements the
window start only when it is greater than zero. Down at ordinal two increments
the window start only while it is less than `total_count - 3`. At the absolute
first or last available row the result stays at that edge and never jumps to
the opposite end. This is a clamped, non-wrapping list. When movement selects
a row, call site `0x00401EC6` invokes exact helper `0x00411450` on the dynamic
10-byte `(id,minX,minY,maxX,maxY)` table at control `+0x10`. The helper returns
the first matching rectangle or four zero coordinates at the `0xFFFF`
terminator, and the caller passes the matched rectangle midpoint to the
already bound cursor-position adapter. It then refreshes the control and
forwards native notification `0x0A` through the current document object's
slot `+0x38`. Evidence type: complete original embedded-runtime bytes for the
365-byte navigation function and 101-byte rectangle lookup, exact call edge,
installed vtable, and previously confirmed dynamic row-ID encoding;
confidence: **Confirmed** for three-row layout, one-row scrolling, clamped
non-wrapping edges, row-rectangle lookup, and cursor centering.

V66 binds the complete original embedded-runtime modal runner
`0x0043FD80` (523 bytes), its direct call at `0x0043FDA9`, and the complete
message pump `0x004103A0` (259 bytes). The runner calls the pump once at the
head of each active modal iteration. It then asks the DirectInput state helper
again for each key binding and tests the current high bit; it does not retain
an edge latch, first-repeat deadline, or fixed repeat interval. A held
direction can therefore dispatch once per completed iteration when its test is
reached. The message pump drains pending Windows messages and, with an active
window, calls `Sleep(0)`; with no active window it calls `Sleep(30)`. This fixes
the source-level repeat policy as level-triggered per modal iteration while
leaving its wall-clock rate dependent on the host message pump and scheduler.
Evidence type: complete original embedded-runtime modal-runner and message-pump
bytes, the exact direct-call edge, imported `KERNEL32.Sleep`, and the already
bound complete DirectInput state helper; confidence: **Confirmed** for
per-iteration level sampling and the active/inactive sleep arguments,
**Unresolved** for a platform-independent millisecond repeat rate.

V67 binds the complete `0x00435850` auxiliary helper (1,339 bytes) and all
three direct call sites at `0x00435140`, `0x0043517F`, and `0x00435361`.
When the choice-record count is nonzero, the helper stores `count - 1` at
window-start offset `+0x424`, toggles display-mode byte `+0x43D` between zero
and one, and either activates document rectangle
`(34,316)-(578,376)` or restores the rectangle saved at `+0x414`. Both paths
perform bounded 640x400 surface/document refresh work and update document
dirty flag bit `0x0002`; neither writes modal result `+8` nor clears modal
running dword `+4`. Modal AREA ID `1`'s special path is therefore confirmed as
a nonterminal presentation-region toggle, not cancel or a separate choice
row. The native visible label for that region remains unresolved. Evidence
type: complete original embedded-runtime helper bytes, all direct-call edges,
fixed object-field writes, document rectangle constants, and the already
bound modal-result/stop fields; confidence: **Confirmed** for the toggle and
its nonterminal status, **Unresolved** for the original visible label.

The audit still does not prove sound, ID `1`'s visible label, ID
`0x0101`/`0x0103` user-facing
meanings, or the meaning of every forwarded notification/result value.

dispatch, bounded mode-1 navigation branches, both direct cursor-adapter calls,

Executable audit `kakyu_ai5_mes_exe_audit/v42` fixes the input-to-list
materialization boundary used by both routine-40 passes. `CAdvSelect` forwards
the command-`0x12` third-expression value to `0x00408E40`. That value indexes
a native group table with 16-byte descriptors. The materializer walks the
selected group's 8-byte records, copies each record's first dword into the
active 4-byte choice vector, and writes the resulting record count at native
offset `+0x20E2`; an empty group publishes count zero and therefore reaches the
already audited `0xFFFF` result path. The second authoritative routine-40
record uses `state_u16[21]` as this key, so the first one-based selection
chooses the second-stage group before slot 13 receives the second one-based
row.

At v42 this proved keyed two-stage selection but did not yet identify the
producer that registers the native groups or the exact records assigned to
each `43C.MES` key. The later v44 producer audit below supersedes that narrower
boundary. The tool still does not infer a 7-by-7 table, invent missing rows, or
enable the reusable bridge for that route. Evidence type: exact
original-runtime call and materializer bytes, hash-bound `LIBLARY.LIB` record
flow, and authoritative `43C.MES` result consumer; confidence: **Confirmed**
for group-key and copy/count mechanics, **Unresolved** at this stage for group
registration, contents, native presentation effects, and gameplay labels.

Executable audit `kakyu_ai5_mes_exe_audit/v44` identifies command `0x10` as
the matching group-record producer. The handler reads its four-byte stored
target, loads the current group selector from manager member `+0x4BC00`, and
indexes a 16-byte descriptor whose record-vector end member begins at
`+0x4BC14`. It appends one 8-byte record through helper `0x0041A5D0`. That
record's first dword is the active script-context pointer from `+0x4B594` plus
the active code coordinate from `+0x4B590`; this is the same first dword that
v42 proved is copied into the active four-byte choice vector. The second dword
is the first parsed expression's evaluated result at parser-relative
`+0x4B6D1`. The handler uses the same `+4` adjusted parser object, so its raw
composite displacement is again `+0x4B6D5`. After registration, the handler
writes the stored target back to the active code-coordinate member.

This closes the generic producer and record-pointer boundary. Audit
`kakyu_mes_routine40_group_route_audit/v1` then makes the complete stored
`43C.MES` address-entry 148 topology reproducible without exporting its text.
The authoritative entry spans `0x479A..0x4FA0`; command-`0x1B` clears groups
`0..6` at `0x479F`, `0x488C`, `0x4ADF`, `0x4AE9`, `0x4D5D`, `0x4DAD`, and
`0x4DB7`. Their command-`0x10` registration counts are respectively
`6, 15, 0, 14, 2, 0, 7`, so groups 2 and 5 are explicitly empty.

Group 0 and groups 4/6 are unconditional. Group 1 IDs `0..14` are individually
guarded by `global_u8[376..390] == 1`. Group 3 IDs `0..12` use
`global_u8[391..395]`, `403`, and `396..402`, each equal to 1. Its ID 13 is
registered when any of the 16 stored flags `2575..2582`, `2997`, or
`2986..2992` is nonzero. Group 6's seven sequential registrations begin at
`0x4DC1` and reach routine 40 at `0x4EC1`, resuming at `0x4EC6`. Every body in
this address entry is one message followed by its exact return target. The
audit rejects a repeated/nonliteral clear, a registration before a group,
invalid body, mismatched guard destination, or a non-unique routine-40 route.

This establishes stored conditional construction, not live gameplay
eligibility. It does not determine which flags are true for a particular
caller, execute native input, assign meanings to group IDs, or establish how
the first one-based selection and second one-based selection combine into a
gameplay outcome. Event Player therefore retains the same fail-closed boundary.
Evidence type: exact original-runtime command-`0x10`/`0x1B` handler bytes, the
v42 materializer, authoritative `43C.MES` SHA-256
`446259e1c34b15de0dbab97c815d83b654fbeb7cca5cd29d4e2498a86706391b`,
and the source-bounded v1 structural audit; confidence: **Confirmed** for the
producer, evaluated group selector, full stored group topology and guards,
descriptor/record strides, and materialized pointer value; **Unresolved** for
live flag provenance, native presentation/input effects, combined result
semantics, and gameplay labels.

Content Core `0.194.0` added the analysis-only contract
`kakyu_mes_routine40_group_preview/v1` around the already confirmed group
mechanics. A contract is admitted only when the reached routine-40 boundary
presents group 0 with `N` rows, the ordered selector set is exactly `0..N`,
every group uses zero-based sequential definition IDs, every body range and
SHA-256 still matches the resolved bytecode, and the total reached count is
unchanged. The first explicit tool row maps only to its same-numbered retained
group. A second explicit row may run that bounded DEF body in a cloned sandbox;
an empty group stops at the native `0xFFFF` list-result boundary. The contract
forbids writes to `state_u16[21]`/`[13]` and forbids caller resume, so it does
not promote 43C to the reusable remake bridge.

The authoritative `43C.MES` address-table entry 148 (`0x479A..0x4FA0`,
routine-40 terminal `0x4EC1`) was re-opened read-only under entry SHA-256
`446259e1c34b15de0dbab97c815d83b654fbeb7cca5cd29d4e2498a86706391b`.
The source-bound validator accepts both the reached default registry
`6/0/0/0/2/0/7` and the maximally eligible registry
`6/15/0/14/2/0/7`, while the six stored command-`0x0E` callers still expose no
activation coordinate or restoration frame. Original launcher audit
`kakyu_ai5_mes_exe_audit/v183` independently rechecked the byte-identical
embedded runtime and retained the keyed group materializer, one-based selected
row, empty-list `0xFFFF`, three visible rows, and clamped non-wrapping
navigation. Evidence type: authoritative `mes.arc` structural replay and
body hashes, configured original launcher/embedded-runtime static audit, plus
synthetic stale-byte/topology tests; confidence: **Confirmed analysis-only
group navigation and body inspection**, **Unresolved** for live 43C host
reachability, conditional gameplay eligibility, native presentation effects,
combined caller outcome, and group-4 fallback meaning.

Content Core `0.161.0` deliberately separates that unresolved native helper
from a reusable remake-side caller-result contract. Schema
`kakyu_mes_routine40_choice_contract/v1` accepts only a reached literal
routine-40 terminal with 2..17 zero-based sequential DEF records, exact body
fingerprints, and the complete immediate one-based
`state_u16[21] == 1..N-1` branch chain reported by DEF-route audit v3. It binds
the definitions, routine resume, comparison coordinates, option entry
coordinates, bytecode fingerprint, and logical source identity. Event Player
revalidates the entire contract against the current resolved bytecode when the
user confirms an option, writes the one-based selection only to slot 21, and
lets the stored MES branch chain select the destination.

This is an **explicit remake input policy**, not a reconstruction of the
original device loop. It does not fabricate the helper's slot-18 result,
slot-13 output, or routine-20 effects, and it does not execute the now-confirmed
manager-only vector clear because its projected registry is execution-local.
It makes no claim about native input bindings, cadence, redraw, or presentation
effects. Audit
v41 independently confirms that its explicit one-based value matches the
native helper's selected-record encoding. The authoritative
archive audit established 573 exact multi-definition consumers that fit this
structural contract. The DENSHA gated matrix, the 43C native-secondary
consumer, and 27 single-definition routes were excluded at v1.
Evidence type: direct authoritative `mes.arc` DEF-route audit v3,
original-executable audit v39, synthetic contract
and stale-source tests, and unchanged full detached-DEF corpus fingerprint;
confidence: **Confirmed remake caller-result bridge** for exact matching
consumers, **Unresolved** for native choice input and omitted native effects.

Content Core `0.363.0` advances the schema to
`kakyu_mes_routine40_choice_contract/v4` and admits a third exact shape: a
**one-based chain reached through one unconditional redirect**. Here the
routine-40's own resume coordinate does not land directly on the
`state_u16[21]` branch chain; it lands on a single unconditional
intra-script jump (command `0x0C`), and that jump's own destination is where
the ordinary one-based chain (or, in principle, the gated matrix) actually
begins. The contract builder now tries the two prior shapes at the resume
coordinate unchanged; only if both fail does it resolve at most one such
jump and retry them from its destination, naming the result
`<prior consumer_kind>_via_unconditional_redirect` and recording the jump's
own source and destination offsets (`redirect_offset`,
`redirect_target_offset`) as two new bound fields. This is confirmed by
execution for all twelve `?_HOTEL.MES` menus - the menu whose case 5 leads
to that heroine's own `?_HOTEL1.MES` handoff (`EP-12`,
`analysis/_undoc/ep12_hotel_menu_report.md`, untracked). For a focused
reproduction, authoritative `A_HOTEL.MES` SHA-256
`793e03ba8cb388ace5269302fbde9bdd90134936a706b40dca577b07143883ed` has its
own first (always-taken under a fresh sandbox) routine-40 call/resume at
`0x1BDB/0x1BE0`, an unconditional jump at `0x1BE5` to `0x1BF9`, and from
there a plain 5-result one-based chain (`option_entry_offsets`
`0x1C08, 0x1EF0, 0x221B, 0x2A52, 0x317A`); each of the twelve heroines
repeats the identical shape at its own offsets, confirmed by execution for
all five registered results in each. Before this call, all twelve menus also
share an unrelated but structurally identical local shape: five
unconditional per-option availability DEF/return pairs each gated by its own
`global_u8[10..14] == 0` check, plus a sixth, longer-bodied option gated by a
special-day compound condition that is false (so unregistered) under this
baseline seed - the 6th definition and the routine-40's own alternate
(mutually exclusive, `global_u8[3004]`-selected) sibling call are read
structurally but not exercised by this contract. `?_HOTEL.MES` additionally
carries, for two heroines (E and I), a second, later routine-40 reached from
a different case than case 5, with its own two-result `44C.MES`/`MACHI.MES`
split; that second question already matches the first (plain one-based)
shape with no redirect and needed no change. Evidence type: authoritative
`mes.arc` structural reads and execution for all twelve `?_HOTEL.MES`
menus, synthetic accept/near-miss tests; confidence: **Confirmed** redirect
consumer shape and offsets for the twelve audited menus, **Unresolved** for
native routine-40 input/selection semantics (unchanged from the two prior
shapes) and for the excluded sixth per-heroine option and alternate
routine-40 call.

Checked against the same family: `DENSHA.MES` carries five routine-40 sites
of its own (code-relative `0xA5C`/2652, `0x1E91`/7825, `0x32FB`/13051,
`0x54C5`/21701 and the already-audited gated matrix at `0x7B02`/31490).
Driven directly from each site's own local DEF cluster (three unconditional,
ungated `DEFINITION` records immediately before the call - e.g. site 1 at
`0x9B4`/2484..`0xA5C`/2652), all five reach a genuine `def_selection_boundary`
and build cleanly: the first four as the **plain one-based chain** (no
redirect; `result_values` `[1, 2, 3]`), the fifth as the already-audited
**gated matrix** (`global_u8[2461]`, values `0/1`). None needs the
unconditional-redirect shape; DENSHA is not a fourth data point for it. A
route that instead resumes at one of these coordinates *after* a prior
segment already executed the site's own three DEFINITIONs, without
re-registering them in the new segment, meets the bounded native
`shared_routine_boundary` stop or a "no catalog choice" refusal - a
resume-carries-no-registered-definitions gap in the multi-hop walk, not a
consumer-shape gap in this contract; it is unrelated to the redirect shape
above and is not addressed here.

The schema bump to v4 that came with the redirect shape does not invalidate
the stored contracts: the 182 `kakyu_mes_routine40_choice_contract/v3`
contracts the committed analysis-group profiles carry stay valid (validated
2026-09-24, Core 0.364.0) because v4 only added the two redirect fields -
`validate()` accepts a v3 contract that carries neither, compares it as if
both were -1, and refuses a v3 contract that carries one. The same day's
first cut refused v3 outright and turned 63 of the 149 `original event
analysis` checks red until this rule; a contract schema bump is checked
against that check, not only the catalog group routes.

Content Core `0.366.0` (EP-12 routine-40 sparse catalog, 2026-09-25) advances
the schema to `kakyu_mes_routine40_choice_contract/v5` and admits a fourth
exact shape - at the *catalog* itself, not the consumer: the reached
definitions list may be **strictly increasing but not contiguous**, ids
`0..max_id` with gaps, as long as every id stays inside `0..MAX_OPTIONS-1`
(16). This is `A_PROMIS.MES:2221`'s own fifteen-place location picker: each
place is declared by its own individually-gated `branch_if_not_true` +
`0x10` DEF pair rather than the uniform `command_1b`/`command_10` run every
prior site used, so under any one seed the interpreter's own trace registers
only the places whose own gate held, at whatever ids those happen to be.
Measured live under the location-0 baseline (guard flag `= 1`, date `0401`,
place-used flags fresh - `docs/spec/mes/promise_groups.md`'s own baseline),
the picker registers ids `0..7,9..13` (thirteen of fifteen places; id 8
needs date `0720..0829`, id 14 needs date `0824` or `1231`, neither holds at
`0401`): `catalog_form: "sparse"`, `hidden_ids: [8]`. The consumer at the
resume coordinate `2236` needed no change at all: it is the unmodified
**plain one-based chain** (`state_u16[21] == 1..12`, `consumer_kind:
one_based_state_u16_21_branch_chain`), because that consumer only ever
matched sequential result positions `1..N`, never the definitions' own ids.
The 2026-09-24 diagnosis that named a parser unable to recognize "the
individually-gated declaration shape" as the blocker
(`docs/spec/tech/content_tools.md`, "a callee with two questions") therefore
overestimated the fix: the interpreter's own execution already resolves
which places register: the sole blocker was `build()`'s own
`definition_id != index` equality, which assumed a contiguous `0..n-1`
catalog. A stored contract now also carries, for each hidden id,
`hidden_gates`: the exact `branch_if_not_true` record (`gate_offset`,
`gate_end`, a SHA-256 of that byte range) a fresh static byte walk finds in
its place - from the lower offered DEF's own registered continuation,
reading each candidate's own `0x10` selector to tell a hidden id's gate from
the next offered id's own gate rather than assuming position, and following
a hidden gate's own encoded false-edge target to the next candidate - so a
re-audit can rehash that exact byte range and confirm the same option stayed
hidden. The walk is purely structural, not a live-trace replay, so it
reproduces identically inside `validate()`'s from-scratch rebuild. A leading
gap (an unoffered id below the first offered one) has no supporting
landmark and is refused rather than guessed; `A_PROMIS.MES`'s own picker has
none, since its first offered id is 0. `result_values` are unchanged - the
one-based consumer positions, not the ids. The v5 bump does not invalidate
the 182 stored `v3` contracts nor any `v4` contract: `validate()` accepts
either without the two new fields (comparing them as absent) and refuses
either carrying one, and `tools/audit_event_analysis_group.py` independently
re-derives `catalog_form`/`hidden_ids` from the definitions list and
re-verifies each `hidden_gates` record's own branch bytes and bounds against
the fresh archive. Evidence type: authoritative `mes.arc` `A_PROMIS.MES`
execution (a throwaway probe, `analysis/ep12_promis_sparse_probe.gd`,
untracked) and synthetic accept/refuse tests; confidence: **Confirmed**
sparse catalog form and the location picker's own offered/hidden ids under
the location-0 baseline, **Unresolved** for native routine-40 input/selection
semantics (unchanged from the three prior shapes) and for producing an
actual `01M <letter> promise` analysis-group profile or catalog entry, which
this change only unblocks and does not itself perform.

Checkpoint C (2026-09-25) produced the twelve profiles and found one more
gap this v5 schema did not itself need to close: `KakyuPlaybackPackageCodeSource`
(the package-only code source `content_core/mes_event_runner.gd` and the
remake both run on) supports `sha256_range` only over a definition's own
recorded body range and the whole-code range - a `hidden_gates` record's own
gate-branch range is neither, so building this contract from a package alone
returned `"Routine-40 hidden-option gate branch cannot be fingerprinted by
this code source"` and stopped every one of the twelve `01m-<letter>-promis`
rows during a package-only playback replay (`original playback package
playback`: 187 rows, 12 stopped) even though the archive-backed replay
reaches each one's real terminal cleanly. The gate hash is an audit aid -
`tools/audit_event_analysis_group.py` always re-verifies it against the
archive, never the package - not something replay execution reads, which
already resolves each candidate from provenance-checked structural records
regardless of the hash. `mes_routine40_choice_contract.gd`'s `build()` now
records `KakyuMesCodeSource.RANGE_UNAVAILABLE` in a hidden gate's own
`gate_condition_sha256` instead of refusing the whole contract when the code
source cannot supply a real one; an archive-backed source (every existing
authoring/audit tool, `tests/test_mes_routine40_choice_contract.gd`'s 39
checks) is unaffected, since `sha256_range` always resolves there. No
playback-package schema field changed - this is purely how the interpreter
reacts to an already-defined "unavailable" sentinel, not a new document
field to serialize - so no `kakyu_playback_package` version move was needed.
Verified: `original playback package playback` 187/187 rows (164 reached a
terminal, 20 place-menu, 3 chain, 0 stopped, from 152/20/3/0-of-175 before
these twelve), `original catalog group routes` and `original event analysis
groups` (173/173) unchanged. Evidence type: the same authoritative-archive
sparse-catalog measurement plus a package-backed replay run before and after
the fix; confidence: **Confirmed** for the fix's correctness on the twelve
measured routes, **Unresolved** for whether another future sparse-catalog
site could need a gate hash for a reason this one does not.

Content Core `0.371.0` (EP-12 TALK, owner ruling 2026-10-04) admits a fourth
exact consumer shape, the **per-position scratch-split chain**
(`consumer_kind: one_based_state_u16_21_scratch_split_branch_chain`), first inside
the `v5` schema; Core `0.372.0` (2026-10-05, advisor ruling) gave it its own schema,
`kakyu_mes_routine40_choice_contract/v6` (below, "The schema is v6"). Measured at the first question of the 96 `?_TALK*.MES` rung
scripts in the state a place calls them in (the heroine's presence flag set
registers the ids `0, 2, 3, 4, 5` - a sparse catalog, `hidden_ids: [1]`;
`docs/spec/mes/talk_family.md`), the consumer is still a one-based chain on
`state_u16[21]`, but a position is either the original chain's pure `== k` row
or **one or more** `state_u16[21] == k and global_u8[c] == v` rows, every row of
one position testing the same cell `c` against a different value `v` (a scratch
cell the script clears at its start; `K_TALK30.MES`: positions 3 and 4 split on
`global_u8[10]` and `[11]`, each into the values 0 and 1, position 5 is the
remaining chain). The builder tries the plain chain and the gated matrix first,
unchanged, and this shape only where both reject, so no site they accepted
moved: every one of the 624 stored contracts of the 199 installed profiles
rebuilds byte for byte (431 `v5` identical, 193 `v3`/`v4` valid). Positions
`1..n-1` are read as rows (each row's false edge leads to the next); position
`n` is the remaining chain, as in the plain chain. The contract records every
row in `comparisons` (a compound row also carries `gate`: `{storage, index,
literal}`), the entry of each position in `option_entry_offsets` (a split
position: its first row's), and the cell of each position in the new key
`position_gates` (`{result, gate: {}}` for a pure position, `{result, gate:
{storage: "global_u8", index, values}}` for a split one); the key exists only
in this shape (`validate()` compares it; a `v3`, `v4` or `v5` contract carrying it
is refused). A position with one compound row means the option is entered only
while that cell holds that value; a mixed position (a pure row among compound
ones), two cells in one position, a repeated value, a gate that is not a
`global_u8` cell and a chain that skips a result are refused. Re-measured over
the 488 questions of the TALK family (the study's probe at the registration
block, four states): fresh, ambient and all-flags states **485 named** as
before, the natural presence state **485 named, from 421** - the 64 rejected
first questions of the rung scripts of C, E, F, G, H, I, K and L are named
(every one `catalog_form: sparse`, `hidden_ids: [1]`) - and the three of
`J_TALK40/50/60` (`33687`, `38723`, `47914`, six registered ids, a first row
that is a pure OR of `state_u16[21]` tests) **stay rejected**. Synthetic proof:
`tests/test_mes_routine40_choice_contract.gd` (accept, revalidate, JSON
transport, execution of both rows of a split position, six near-miss refusals,
the non-`global_u8` refusal and its control). Evidence type: authoritative
`mes.arc` execution and decode (scratch probes under `analysis/_undoc/`,
untracked) and synthetic accept/refuse tests; confidence: **Confirmed** for the
64 named questions and the unchanged installed contracts, **Unresolved** for
what writes the split cells (inferred: the registering definitions) and for
J's six-id shapes (measured, not diagnosed).

**The schema is v6 (Core `0.372.0`, EP-12 TALK, advisor ruling 2026-10-05).** The
`position_gates` key had been added inside `v5` at `0.371.0`, before any contract of
the form was installed; the shape change is versioned like the earlier ones

The paired-character presentation path is separately bounded. Opcode-table
command `0x01` reaches embedded native handler `0x004184E0`; outer-dispatch

reading beyond the entry. Instruction v18 records this as
`native_handler_family=double_byte_character_stream_presentation` and
`native_stream_consumption=double_byte_pairs_until_nul_or_nonlead`. It also
records whether the existing CP932 text projection ends at the same consumed

The refined pass retained 888,437 stream tokens: 666,962 single-byte and

Command `0x0D` has a single-byte dispatch token with no opcode-specific
operand. Jump-table entries
`0x02`, `0x0D`, and `0x12` all reach the wrapper at engine virtual address
`0x004181F2`, which invokes the same CCommon virtual slot without reading an
opcode-specific operand. All three checked manager vtables (`0x0047A87C`,
`0x0047B6FC`, and `0x0047E074`) place `0x004187C0` in that slot. This is not a
no-op handler: it repeatedly invokes the active script stream callback, tests
the returned byte against the native CP932 lead ranges, calls the character
draw path for ordinary bytes, updates message cursor fields, wraps within the
configured text rectangle, and can issue a rectangle operation before return.
RTTI identifies the active byte source as `CScript`; its vtable at
`0x0047DF74` places `0x0043D540` in slot `+0x0C`. That callback returns the
byte at the current source pointer plus index and advances the pointer by its
argument. Argument `0` is therefore a non-advancing peek and argument `1`
consumes exactly one byte. With that contract, `0x004187C0` is bounded: it
consumes and presents consecutive single bytes, consumes a terminating NUL,
and returns before an `0x81..0x9F` or `0xE0..0xEF` lead without consuming the
lead. Its inner loop does not classify `0xFA..0xFC` as leads even though the
outer dispatcher does, so the probe preserves that distinction.

The wrapper's lack of an explicit operand proves only the dispatch-token
width; the handler may consume the following bounded run. Content Core records
`native_handler_family=character_stream_presentation`,
`native_stream_consumption=single_byte_run_until_nul_or_primary_double_byte_lead`,
and a limit-bounded probe with the consumed count, stop coordinate, and stop
reason. Event Runner trace v27 reports commands `0x02` and `0x12` as explicit
fail-closed `native_presentation_boundary` results unless an exact already-
traced dialogue trailer gives command `0x02` its narrower continuation role.
The native boundary retains the probe but does not consume it as simulated
dialogue or reproduce display/cursor effects. Its `0x0D` fallthrough is only a
bounded structural projection with the same omitted native effects.

`d3ea01755943573b9241f65a8a1373111959210007824eac33d29104e0afcc7b`.

selection boundary at `0x96D4`. Other `0x0E` record shapes remain

`0x00419210`, parser slot `+0x60`, the record-result C-string copy from native
workspace `+0x4B6AD` through raw manager displacement `+0x4B55C` into the
actual direct `CScript +0x4B558` buffer pointer, receiver
virtual calls `+0x20` and `+0x58`, and presentation flag `+0x20BC` mask `8`.
It resolves those calls to the three public-context vtables. Slot `+0x20`
receives the active-string pointer as its first argument; that pointer is
outside the implementation's `0..5` switch and takes the default cleanup

primary/common notification implementations. The audit fixes all 15 flag-bit
read sites and all three writer sites. The stream reader clears the bit in
mode 1, resets stream coordinate `+0x4B58C`, not MES coordinate `+0x4B590`,
notifies, and resumes byte dispatch. Neither the handler nor these checked

`+0x64` virtual-base adjustment, the `0x3194`-byte active-buffer lifecycle, and

identity, dispatcher/three-vtable/handler disassembly, and full headless corpus

The authoritative archive contains 1,249 instances across 273 MES entries;

`EVENTD05.MES:0x173B`, whose target is `MACHI.MES`. In the latter route the

continuing byte dispatch. No checked path writes the active MES coordinate,

The full reload case replays bounded notification with the reloaded state
pointer but contains no MES coordinate write, script-runner call, or caller

`0x004137E6`. The first lies in the three-context iterator extent
`0x00402054..0x004023E9`; the other four lie in the `CBGSelect` stack-context

The same v53 audit binds five CScript-family method vtables at
`0x0047A8EC`, `0x0047B76C`, `0x0047CDD4`, `0x0047DF74`, and `0x0047E0E4`.
MSVC RTTI identifies them respectively as adjusted `CAI5Doc`, `CCommon`,
`CFunc`, `CScript`, and `CScriptManager` subobjects at complete-object offsets
`0x22608`, `0x48`, `0x225A0`, `0`, and `0x225E8`; their hierarchy descriptors
report 9, 3, 3, 2, and 7 base-class records. They are therefore one shared
script/document class family, not five unrelated active-string consumers.
V53 binds all five base-class arrays and every referenced base descriptor.
The `CAI5Doc` hierarchy contains `ISystemInfo` and `CScriptManager`;
`CScriptManager` contains `CFunc` and `CCommon`; both of those branches reach
virtual `CScript` and `CThread` bases. The audited PMD adjustments include the
`CAI5Doc`-view `CScriptManager`/`CFunc` displacement `+0x8`, its `CCommon`
displacement `+0x225A0`, and the standalone `CScriptManager`-view `CCommon`
displacement `+0x22598`. This fixes ownership topology and adjustment data,
but it does not by itself establish a runtime active-string handoff.
The same audit fixes the unique construction route at
`0x00405214..0x0040524A`: the application allocates a `0x72C98`-byte
`CAI5Doc`, calls its constructor at `0x00405231`, and stores the result in its
document member at `+0xE8`. `CAI5Doc` construction calls the `CScript`
constructor for subobject `+0x22608` and the `CScriptManager` constructor for
subobject `+8`; the manager constructs `CFunc` at its root and `CCommon` at
`+0x22598`. `0x00405231` is the only direct call to this `CAI5Doc`

Audit v84 follows the distinct top-level flag-8 path in `CScript::run` at

### Command `0x09` and token `0xF6` address one storage (Core 0.377.0)

Command `0x09`'s dword stores (`0x00418CBD` and `0x00418D05`, handler
`0x00418C60`) and expression token `0xF6`'s read (`0x004060A6`) address the same
original storage, `common_state + 0x3000 + index * 4`. The receiver
displacements differ at the two sites and reduce to the same common
virtual-base field after their respective `this` adjustments. Temporary
arguments and `global_i32` are therefore not separate original storage
domains: what a command `0x09` writes at index `n` is what `global_i32[n]`
reads, for any later reader in any routine or script. Evidence type: configured
original executable audit (the `0x09` handler and its three-vtable routing,
configured-original audit v37's reconfirmation of the indexed writer, and the
token-`0xF6` evaluator site; first recorded in [Audio](audio.md), "Native SE,
argument storage, and polling evidence"); confidence: **Confirmed**.

Event Runner models it since Core 0.377.0 (TD-56): command `0x09` writes each
value through the sandbox into `global_i32` (trace rows carry `write_storage =
"global_i32"`, `write_start`, `write_count` and `write_bank`, beside the
existing `argument_slot_*` fields), and the two argument readers, routine `0`'s
message record id and routine `23`'s BGM selector, read `global_i32[1]` from the
sandbox whoever wrote it (a command `0x09`, a command `0x0A`, or a caller's
seed). Tool decisions, not original facts:

1. **Representation.** The runner's `argument_slots` dictionary survives only as
   per-run provenance (which indices a command `0x09` or `0x16` wrote, and the
   value written), for traces, previews and continuations. It is never read for
   meaning, and a continuation restoring it does not re-impose it over the
   storage. A nested script's callee therefore leaves its `0x09` writes visible
   after the caller frame returns, as one shared storage implies.
2. **The unwritten value.** The original's value of an index before its first
   write is not established. A sandbox that has not written `global_i32[1]`
   reads the sandbox's `0`. The former "slot 1 unwritten" gate is gone: routine
   `0` then yields message id `0`, and routine `23` stops at the unmapped
   selector `0` (fail closed, no write) instead of falling to a shared-routine
   boundary.
3. **Command `0x16` stays out and is unresolved.** Its handler stores the dword
   at native state base `+0x20EC + slot * 4` (above); no audit relates that base
   to `common_state + 0x3000`, and nothing reads the index it writes in the
   corpus (it occurs 39 times in 4 entries; in the replays its one slot-`9` run
   executes 78 times at `LIBLARY.LIB:61115`, and nothing reads
   `global_i32[9]`). It stays argument-slot only.
4. **The reference index is unchanged.** `references.state` still carries no
   write row for `0x09` (see "State reference index completes the write runs"
   below), so the frozen instruction-v45 digest does not move; extending the
   index is deferred.
5. **The EVENTB03 adapter** (disposable staging of slots `1` and `2` before
   routine `9`) is now a no-op projection of equal values and stays unchanged;
   its retirement, with its audits' re-pin, is a separate decision.
6. **The event definitions do not take the argument storage as an event
   effect (D11, owner ruling 2026-10-11).** The runner's `global_i32[1]` and
   `[2]` rows are the arguments a caller hands a routine, so the definition
   producers (`tools/project_event_definition.py`, `ArgumentStorage`, used by
   the v4, v5 and v6 paths and so by v7) leave a run's `global_i32` net change
   out of the effect derivation (no `after` row, no witness row) when the run
   executed a command-`0x09` record whose write range covers the index and
   whose literal equals the change's final value, or, in a flow variant, an
   earlier hop of the same variant did. They record it once per
   `(index, value)` in `unresolved`, naming the smallest covering record. A
   `global_i32` change with no such record, such as an expression-valued
   `0x09`, keeps the ordinary path. The persistent flags that the library
   ladders now set (`global_u8[4000]`, `[4090]`, `[4091]` = 1) are not argument
   storage and enter the definitions as ordinary effects. This is a projection
   tool decision, not a native claim; it rests on C2's read-coverage evidence:
   every library-ladder read of an index follows a command `0x09` that wrote it
   in the same run (6,681 reads) or in an earlier hop of the same flow variant
   (134), and every `global_i32` row gained in the replays has a covering
   `0x09` executed in its run or variant (`analysis/_undoc/td56/`, untracked).
   The rule reads the v3 replays' `executed` offsets and is inert on a v2
   replay, the input of the frozen v4 to v6 producers.

Effect on the corpus (measured over the 227 analysis-group replays, 12,871 runs):
messages, message counts, terminals and resource rows do not change; `state_diff`
gains `global_i32` rows (index `1` in 8,316 runs and `2` in 138; the two-line
mirror that C0 prototyped also wrote index `9` in 39 runs because it mirrored
command `0x16` too, which this model does not) and, where
`LIBLARY.LIB` routines 9 and 27 now see the caller's selector instead of `0`,
the library path, its executed offsets and a few downstream cells change. The
243,455 slot-1 reads by routines `0` and `23` are equal under the old and the new
reading, so the corpus does not distinguish an argument-slot mirror from the
alias; the alias is the original's rule and is what authored or edited routes
(a seeded index `1`, a command `0x0A` write) need. An independent check from
the original side: the EVENTB03 result-3 route's six routine-9 calls
(selectors 69, 68, 69, 68, 68, 69 in source order, [Audio](audio.md), "EVENTB03
result-3 SE occurrences") reach the `KSE00131.WAV` and `KSE00130.WAV` rungs
(`LIBLARY.LIB:0x1103` and `0x10D9`) in exactly that order under the alias;
the selector-0 ladder reached neither. Measurement: `analysis/_undoc/td56/`
(untracked).

### P2-05 Host-Activation Investigation Contract

The remaining command-`0x0E` question is an ownership and activation-contract
problem, not an instruction-byte coverage target. The preceding audits close
the literal direct references, direct-base and field-first aliases, known
script-family vtable cells, bounded startup/root-stream installation and
re-entry, fixed presentation/transition paths, and multiple conservative
indirect-call families. Audit v267 finds no new product from the 7,936-byte
bound through the exact 8,999-byte pre-candidate boundary, and audit v268
classifies the sole 9,000-byte product as a cross-return native-object false
association. Those are bounded results; neither their count nor a scan of
every byte in the 610,304-byte embedded runtime would establish the missing
host behavior.

P2-05 may be promoted only when reproducible original-source evidence connects
all of the following obligations:

1. the retained target name and the authoritative command record that produced
   it;
2. the host phase or loop edge that consumes the request;
3. archive selection, entry lookup, and destination stream ownership;
4. installation of that stream into the executing script family;
5. the code-relative intro coordinate selected for the new stream;
6. caller/context ownership across the handoff; and
7. return restoration or a proven terminal/root replacement.

The next static method is a bidirectional slice. The forward half starts at the
authoritative command-`0x0E` producers and the retained-name/flag writes, then
follows aliases across function returns, host modes, and message/root-loop
boundaries. The backward half starts at the confirmed MES loader, stream
installer, code-coordinate writes, and `CScript::run` sites, then recovers the
owning document/script receiver and caller chain. A new scanner form is
justified only when this slice identifies a concrete unrepresented alias,
spill, or call-frame shape.

Audit v268 closes the existing distance-scanner lineage by classifying the
single product admitted at 9,000 bytes. Unconditional distance widening stops
there. If the bounded static slices do not connect, the runtime must continue
to expose a typed `external_host_activation` boundary, dependent routes must
remain partial or blocked, and one later original-runtime debugger batch should
watch the retained target/flag and break on load, stream install, coordinate
write, and script run. A negative scan cannot complete P2-05 or justify an
invented activation coordinate.

Evidence type: synthesis of the already documented, hash-bound original
embedded-runtime audits and read-only authoritative `mes.arc` command-route
cross-checks; no new opcode meaning, archive coordinate, or runtime execution
claim is introduced by this investigation contract. Confidence:
**Confirmed** for the listed bounded exclusions, the no-delta interval through
8,999, and the sole 9,000-byte product classification; **Unresolved** for the
arbitrary retained-target consumer, activation coordinate/context, and caller
restoration.

Host-activation slice audit v1 turns this investigation contract into one

`44C.MES` address entries 334, 337, and 340 at `0xB167`, `0xB2A6`, and
`0xB4F3`; and `L_HOTEL2.MES` address entry 106 at `0x3345`. It binds those

### Ghidra route-facts triage boundary

The hash-bound 610,304-byte embedded runtime was additionally imported into a
local Ghidra 12.1.3 project through the tracked headless route-facts exporter.
For the exact v312 seventy-four-route inventory, recovered function ownership
places 67 routes across more than one containing function. Only route indices
45 through 51 keep all six candidate sites in one recovered function,
`0x00440380`: they begin at load `0x0044069B` and end at call `0x0044095C`
for index 45 or `0x00440C99` for indices 46 through 51. All 74 final call sites
produce normalized high-p-code facts and a bounded indirect-call target
definition tree. The local JSON is intentionally untracked and contains no MES
payload.

This is an evidence-routing result, not a new original semantic rule. Ghidra's
function recovery and decompiler normalization are independent heuristic
analysis; they can prioritize byte-level false-association review but cannot
by themselves prove register ownership, loader identity, host activation, or
caller restoration. Exact original-EXE bytes, the existing route inventory,
and authoritative `43C.MES` producer cross-audit remain the deciding evidence.
Evidence type: read-only original executable hash check, exact embedded-runtime
hash, Ghidra recovered function/basic-block ownership, normalized p-code, and
source hash recheck. Confidence: **Confirmed** for reproducible tool output and
its `67 / 7` partition; **Unresolved** for the semantic meaning of the seven
same-function products and for P2-05 host activation.

missed direct function call joins the bounded command handler to load/install/
run.

`65812255c68c5bb293cff2577e2e4718e2bc8195766604e38c616c0a18ea82e0`.

### Ghidra dbgeng runtime-trace preparation boundary

The original P2-05 evidence batch was represented by the source-audited

return-classification correction below. Its generator reopens the
authoritative `mes.arc` and original launcher, reruns the exact executable and

in memory, and emits an untracked local debugger plan. For representative
target `43C.MES`, the fresh archive pass retains the 42,678-byte entry and all

`65812255c68c5bb293cff2577e2e4718e2bc8195766604e38c616c0a18ea82e0`.

The checked embedded runtime is a 32-bit x86 PE32 image with preferred image
base `0x00400000` and `DYNAMIC_BASE` clear. The plan nevertheless expresses all
twenty-four software breakpoints as module-base-relative RVAs. Four staged x86
hardware watchpoints cover the retained target's first dword read, presentation
flag write, active-state pointer replacement, and MES code-coordinate write.
The breakpoint/watchpoint observations are grouped under the existing seven
proof obligations: target identity, host consumption timing, archive lookup,
stream installation, intro coordinate, caller/context ownership, and return or
terminal behavior. Promotion requires one target-qualified session that joins
all seven; startup-baseline or negative hits do not qualify.

The nineteenth software breakpoint is the executable-audited
primary-1/secondary-21 result store at `0x00414DC5`. Immediately before
`mov word [edi+0x20A8], ax`, `EDI` is the active state and low `AX` is the
mode-1 helper's one-based result. The collector accepts this as
`target_choice_result` only after target execution begins on the qualified
owner thread and `EDI` still equals the retained target state; it also
normalizes the current stream pointer to a code-relative coordinate. This
diagnostic observation is not part of the seven host-activation obligations.

The first target-qualified replay with that breakpoint completed 7/7 while

site `0x0043532E`. Immediately before `mov [esi+8], eax`, `ESI` is the modal
control and `EAX` carries the one-based selected-record result. The collector
promotes this hit only during the matching owner-thread target run with a valid
active stream coordinate. This broader observation remains diagnostic and
does not alter the seven proof obligations.

The subsequent complete row-3 replay did not hit the common modal copy either.
The twenty-first breakpoint moves earlier to the audited selected-control
result store at `0x00401CF7`. The control maps the zero-based host row, adds

That earlier advanced-control store also remained untouched in a fourth
complete row-3 EVENTB03 replay. Executable audit
`kakyu_ai5_mes_exe_audit/v313` therefore supplies a distinct standard-message
candidate separate from command-`0x12`. The exact `CNormalSelect` vtable at

Evidence type: exact original-runtime RTTI/vtable and instruction bytes,
target-qualified original-engine capture, and operator row-3 observation;

negative separation from the three advanced-control sites, **Unresolved** for

The fifth complete row-3 replay did not execute that twenty-second breakpoint.

Collector reports additionally expose `target_choice_probe_diagnostics`.

`kakyu_mes_runtime_trace_capture/v3` consumes plan v3 with an explicit PID or
an opt-in auto-selection that requires exactly one full-file hash match. It

matches four independent 16-byte code-window hashes at the receiver call, MES

ASCII resource names. Raw memory is excluded by default. Explicit
`--capture-state-snapshots` mode adds only the matching target start and first
stream-qualified target-return or root-replacement

start is normalized only from a matching fresh run entry or the constrained
same-owner flag-8 resume described above. A caller run return before matching

target start, a matching owner return on a different active code base becomes
`target_nested_run_return`; only a receiver/state match on the installed target
base becomes `target_run_return`. A complete same-owner command-`0x0E` successor
chain becomes `target_root_replacement`; unrelated or nested loads do not. The
default stops at the first qualified terminal, while
`--continue-after-matching-return` records further activity after a target
return until another terminal, event limit, timeout, or operator interruption.
The collector removes its breakpoints and attempts detach in `finally`.

source-bound module gates, fail-closed execution normalization, live reachability
through the same-owner resume, and stream-aware return classification;
**Confirmed** for the EVENTB03 root-replacement terminal; **Unresolved** for a
distinct stream-qualified full EVENTB03 return path, if one exists.

An additional EVENTB03 replay with debugger output restored also yielded zero
target events: stop-file polling had shortened every dbgeng wait to one second,

### EVENTB03 target-start preset reduction

`audit_mes_runtime_trace_preset.py` v4 provides a path-free reduction layer
between local debugger snapshots and a future Event Player preset. It accepts
only target-qualified capture schemas v2/v3, requires exactly one
`target_execution_start` snapshot per input, and checks the capture's archive,
original-executable, target-entry, snapshot-size, and snapshot hashes against
sources reopened read-only during the audit. It reruns original executable
audit v317 before interpreting the buffer: `global_u8` begins at native state
offset `+0x80`, `state_u16` at `+0x2084`, and bank-zero `banked_u16` at the
pointer target `+0x20B8`. The native allocation is 12,692 bytes; the collector
retains only its bounded first `0x3000` bytes, which cover the audited fields.

The reducer walks valid authoritative target CFG condition ASTs and accepts
only literal indices in those three storage families. It keeps unresolved
decoder conditions visible and refuses v4 promotion unless the target is 100%
structurally aligned with no unresolved condition coordinate. It also scans
every decoded target operand for references in the three captured storage
families and reports other storage families without assigning them snapshot
semantics. Its report
contains no `data_hex`, dialogue, payload, or absolute source path. It groups
field values across captures into stable target-local candidates, surrounding
host-context observations, stable-zero omission candidates, runtime-owned
choice fields, and variable fields. The
evidence does not support copying the whole snapshot as an authored input, but
the target-local set is still labeled
`source_qualified_target_local_input_candidate`
with `promotion_ready=false`: observational equality cannot prove causal
minimality, shared-routine sufficiency, or native presentation behavior.

Structured IR v4 removes ten former EVENTB03 empty-stack condition
projections. Each came from decoding a confirmed `0x0D/0x0B` surface record
body as a command-`0x0B` branch after a preceding `0x0D/0x09` MMO envelope was
split incorrectly. With both presentation envelopes retained, authoritative
EVENTB03 has 32 distinct valid condition coordinates, zero unresolved
condition coordinates, and a 100% structurally aligned code projection. This
does not assign native surface semantics beyond the separately audited bounded
operations.

Applied to nine qualified EVENTB03 row-3 starts from the unchanged source set,
v4 observes stable context `state_u16[4]=6`, `[7]=0413`, and `[19]=1825`.
Its complete target-operand scan covers 2,237 decoded instruction identities
and 174 references across 14 captured-storage fields; none names `[4]`, `[7]`,
or `[19]`. V4 therefore publishes the three values only as surrounding-host
context observations and emits an empty target-local candidate field set.
`banked_i32` occurs in target operands but remains explicitly outside the
three mapped snapshot storage families.
Although all snapshots enter with `[8]=3`, authoritative
`EVENTB03.MES:0x0106..0x010B` writes `[8]=0` before its first condition at
`0x010B`; v4 reports this as a precondition literal overwrite instead of a
portable preset field. It also excludes six all-zero direct fields and
runtime-owned `[21]`; it records `[12]=224/254` and
`banked_u16[0][210]=49..52` as variable rather than inventing exact preset
values. Evidence type: authoritative `EVENTB03.MES` CFG decode, original
executable audit v317, nine target-qualified original-engine snapshots, and
source hash rechecks. Confidence: **Confirmed** for source identity, native
field mapping, and observed value sets; **Unresolved** for causal minimality of
omitted native presentation and complete playable reconstruction.

The companion six-case matrix verifies the called-library paths as well as
their main-script resumes. EVENTB03 call `0x00FC` reaches routine 28 with
argument slot 1 equal to 1 and the LIBLARY coordinate sequence
`0x02D0/0x02D7/0x02E2/0x0304/0x030F/0x032B/0x0347/0x03EA`. Call `0x0225`
reaches routine 21 with argument 1 and sequence
`0x03F2/0x0417/0x041E/0x0429/0x0430`. Call `0x0235` reaches routine 28 with
argument 0 and the shorter sequence
`0x02D0/0x02D7/0x02E2/0x0304/0x0347/0x03EA`. Call `0x08DF` reaches the same
routine-21 sequence with argument 46635. Every call preserves its argument and

## Archive-Wide Aligned Native Payload Boundary

Content Core `0.197.0` introduced the aligned regional decoder used by the
static MES analysis index for an outer command `0x0D` native single-byte probe
beginning with command-looking byte `0x0B` or `0x0C`. Content Core `0.210.0`
supersedes that lead-only test: the exact instruction plus probe-consumed bytes
form one `[start,end)` record whenever the handler-consumed run contains a
`0x0B` or `0x0C` at any position. The command byte retains its normal typed
metadata; the suffix is retained as `bounded_byte_preserving_opaque_stream`
with its own start, end, length, raw identity, and every internal shadow-control
coordinate. The decoder resumes only at the probe end, so a consumed internal
byte cannot become a sibling branch or continuation instruction.

This rule is deliberately narrow. A generic native probe is not sufficient
evidence that every following byte belongs to that dispatch, and a trial broad
promotion changed otherwise valid instruction alignment. The aligned decoder
therefore does not consume other probe shapes. Confirmed MMO, voice, AX,
surface, common-record, and presentation-control envelopes continue to use
their existing exact typed boundaries; new noncanonical forms remain
fail-closed evidence work.

The read-only authoritative `mes.arc` pass finds 332 aligned control-shaped
native payload records totaling 2,247 suffix bytes. Reproducible examples are
`06C.MES:0xA0B5..0xA0BC` with owned suffix
`0xA0B6..0xA0BC`, and `27C_EV.MES:0x0141..0x014A` with suffix
`0x0142..0x014A`. The boundary defect found from the MD-02 transfer audit is
`D_DATE2.MES` address-table `entry_0114` (`0x4081..0x40DD`): the outer record
at `0x40AE..0x40B6` owns its complete native suffix `0x40AF..0x40B6`, including
the internal control-looking byte at `0x40B3`, and real text resumes at
`0x40B6`. The former sibling projection interpreted that internal coordinate
as an out-of-code continuation to `0x820100FF`; v43 no longer emits that node.
The same pass retains 1,251 strict-analysis stops as explicit
`opaque_region_tail` ranges totaling 734,485 bytes. Each range records its
region, exact coordinates, raw hex, SHA-256, and
`byte_preserving_fail_closed` policy; it is not decoded again as sibling MES.

The historical instruction-v43 / analysis-v19 baseline indexed
2,389,424 instructions, 220,491 message
rows, 185,674 code references, 521,125 state references, and
36,149 resource references across all 1,016 MES/LIB entries. Every message is
owned by a typed `text` or `dispatcher_character_text` instruction. The
archive-wide negative-space audit reports zero message starts inside aligned
native payloads, expression spans, or opaque tails. The pre-existing 30 CP932
diagnostics remain byte diagnostics rather than promoted dialogue, and no
accepted message uses a native-incompatible `0xF0..0xF9` lead. The archive
fingerprint is unchanged.

Evidence type: direct read-only authoritative archive parse with the shared
container, exact `D_DATE2.MES` entry/range handoff before and after the change,
strict/aligned instruction decoder and raw-boundary hash checks, message-owner
negative-space audit, and original-executable audit v317. The original handler
at `0x004187C0` consumes the single-byte run through its NUL or defers at a
primary double-byte lead; the record rule does not infer a native effect from
the consumed bytes. Offsets are code-relative; confidence is **Confirmed** for
the exact aligned and opaque `[start,end)` ranges, removal of the shadow
continuation, and exclusion from the static string index. Native display
effects and the semantic meaning of opaque bytes remain **Unresolved**.

edges, expansion limits, explicit decode stops, and truncation diagnostics
from the editor-only `kakyu_mes_reference_graph_export/v1` wrapper. Phase 5

## Cross-Language Framing Equivalence

Phase 1-4 authority is moving to Python by the owner's decision in
`../tech/product_roles.md`, and authority is MA-09's measurement rather than the
language that computes it. The measurement that crosses the language line is
record framing: the exact `[start, end)` of every consumed instruction and every
byte-preserving opaque remainder. `export_mes_framing_digest.gd` emits the
authoritative framing as a canonical line list and
`audit_mes_framing_equivalence.py` measures the Python decoder against it, so a
divergence reduces to one coordinate and the opcode there.

**Measured 2026-09-06 over `mes.arc`
`31a95b31cb0f1051cf973a4dba4f4a5405671e4488240adfafb9b02290986aa6`, 1,016
entries and 2,386,774 records: sequential framing equivalence on 1,016 of 1,016
entries, per-record agreement 1.0000, no entry opaque on one side only, and no
command left unframed.** The audit's `--require-equivalent` reading passes.

The distance closed in five steps, and each was a shared mechanism rather than a
command. Eight commands share one record-list grammar, so `0x1B` — named as the
sequential blocker at 58.2% — moved with `0x1D`, `0x0E`, `0x0F`, `0x10`, `0x11`,
`0x12` and `0x15`. `0x01` and the bytes above `0x1F` are one character-stream
probe. Nine write-run commands differ only in the header before one shared
`(expression, continuation byte)` pair run. `0x0D`'s confirmed-form tree is the
whole of that command's framing. Two were corrections rather than coverage:
`0x0B` read five raw bytes where the authority reads a u32 target, framing all
71,165 of its records one byte long and, being a branch, desynchronizing
everything after it; and `0x0C` framed correctly while handing back four
separate bytes that a consumer reassembled by hand.

The last step was the expression parser, and it is the one worth stating
precisely. Framing had already agreed on every individual record while 495
entries still diverged sequentially, because agreement per record and agreement
on a whole entry are different questions. The authority parses strictly and
fails closed when a terminator arrives with a stack depth other than one, which
ends the region as a byte-preserving opaque span; the Python parser recorded
that as a diagnostic and kept decoding, emitting instructions inside bytes the
authority had declared opaque. Two narrower bounds differed with it: the scan
must stop at `MAX_EXPRESSION_BYTES` from the expression start whatever the
caller allows, and every operand read is bounded by the expression's own limit
rather than by the surrounding buffer. Strict parsing is the framing decoder's
mode; the permissive mode remains the structural one used for analysis.

**This closes the Phase 2 gate in Python and does not by itself move the Phase
1-4 authority.** That authority is the whole MA-09 handoff — container, typed
and opaque IR, references, CFGs, calls and trace — with the owner-approved v45
corpus fingerprint `fae349f9...eab6f5` above as its target. Framing is one
component of it. Until an equivalent
Python handoff result is recorded, `../../../todo/mes_pipeline.md`'s operating
rule stands as written and GDScript remains the Phase 1-4 producer.

`mes_handoff_transport.py` supplies common normalization and canonical JSON
bytes for production and verification. It reproduces the GDScript
full-precision decimal representation; Python's ordinary shortest float
spelling is insufficient for fingerprint equality. The bounded integer
arithmetic implementation and its decimal interval selection require no engine
or third-party runtime. Dictionaries use string keys without coercion, sorted
by key, and packed byte arrays use the existing hex object. The accepted subset
is finite binary64 floats, signed 64-bit integers, Unicode scalar strings,
booleans, null, lists, dictionaries and packed bytes. Standard JSON control
escapes are supported; other C0 controls, including GDScript's nonstandard
vertical-tab escape, are rejected so Python consumers can read every exported
payload. Cycles, unsupported types, invalid Unicode and non-string keys fail
closed. Per-call limits are 256 nesting levels, 4,000,000 normalized nodes and
256 MiB of canonical UTF-8. These are Python transport limits, not assertions
about original MES semantics or general Godot Variant serialization.

## Archive-Wide Record Alignment Closure

Content Core `0.198.0` adds the independent
`kakyu_mes_record_alignment_audit/v1` projection. It partitions every
bootstrap and address-table region, decodes only through the structural aligned
API, and then verifies that each typed instruction's declared byte length and
raw hex match one contiguous source range. If structural decoding stops, the
remaining region becomes one `byte_preserving_fail_closed` opaque tail with
exact coordinates, raw bytes, and SHA-256. Typed records plus opaque tails must
cover the container code exactly once; overlap, gaps, or a changed source
fingerprint fail the audit.

The read-only authoritative pass covers all 1,016 MES/LIB entries and 134,475
bootstrap/address regions. All 18,079,488 code bytes are framed: 2,478,500
typed instructions own 18,079,431 bytes, while one 57-byte opaque tail owns the
remainder. The tail is `08C.MES` address-table `entry_0032`, code-relative
`0x0E62..0x0E9B`; structural decoding stops at a command-`0x0A` destination
expression stack underflow. Its bytes are retained without attempting sibling
commands, and its native or gameplay meaning remains unresolved.

The same inventory contains 358,924 compound records totaling 3,842,271
bytes. It covers all confirmed typed record-list commands and presentation
families, including 1,047 aligned control-shaped native guards, 7,645 MMO marker
records, selectors 2/6/7/8, selector-0 AX bindings, and subcommand-10 mode-1
records. Counts are grouped by family and entry in the path-free corpus report;
the 1,047 structural guards span 149 entries, while 332 are reached by the
strict static-analysis projection. Noncanonical forms do not inherit a
neighboring family rule. The indexed-intro
Event Runner baseline still has no generic unsupported-opcode, decoder, write,
or target failures, and the analysis-corpus string audit still owns all 220,491
messages with zero native, expression, or opaque overlap.

Evidence type: direct read-only authoritative `mes.arc` container and aligned
decoder audit, exact source-slice comparisons, SHA-256 opaque preservation,
the unchanged-source fingerprint check, and the previously documented
archive/EXE qualification for each promoted native presentation family.
Offsets are code-relative. Confidence is **Confirmed** for complete byte
partition, exact compound `[start,end)` ranges, fail-closed opaque retention,
and string negative space; **Unresolved** for the 57-byte tail's semantics and
for actual native pixel, input, cadence, or audio effects. This closes MA-08
and the Phase 2 and Phase 3 gates without claiming those native effects.

## Corpus Transfer-Direction Audit

Content Core `0.210.0` reserves
`kakyu_mes_transfer_direction_audit/v1`. The GDScript corpus tool accepts only
current container and analysis schemas, builds and verifies each Phase 1--4
handoff, and scans only typed `branch_if_not_true` and
`continuation_transfer` operands. It classifies each target by numeric
direction and address-table-region relation. Opaque tails are counted but are
explicitly outside the scanned transfer set.

Against the unchanged authoritative archive, 1,016 entries contain 113,613
typed transfers: conditional false targets are 35,645 same-region forward and
35,370 cross-region forward; continuations are 17,740 same-region forward,
21,055 cross-region forward, 373 same-region backward, and 3,430 cross-region
backward. There is no backward typed conditional and no invalid target. The 373
same-region backward continuations occur across 106 entries; `MACHI.MES`
contains 109. The deterministic report fingerprint is
`5ebe345d0fb8e8e7088cb295b1f909cb45d5c001fafc8ebc24ef4b48a75bf6ba`.

This is a candidate reduction, not a natural-loop proof. A later MD-02 pass
must build a complete same-region CFG, check entry coverage and dominance, and
retain label/goto fallback whenever a hidden, opaque, jump-table, call/return,
or external-entry edge prevents proof. The 1,251 strict opaque tails totaling
734,485 bytes remain unresolved and forbid an archive-wide claim that no other
backward native or opaque transfer exists. Evidence type: repeated direct
read-only authoritative-archive traversal, current handoff verification,
focused `D_DATE2.MES` boundary audit, exact target/range classification, report
fingerprinting, and unchanged-source hash check. Confidence is **Confirmed**
for the typed transfer inventory and candidate coordinates; loop, dispatcher,
and call/return semantics remain **Unresolved**.

## Phase 5 Lossless Linear Decompiler IR

Content Core `0.203.0` reserves `kakyu_mes_decompiler_ir/v1`, produced offline
by `tools/decompile_mes_handoff.py`. The Python lifter accepts only an intact,
schema-exact `kakyu_mes_analyzer_handoff/v1`; it does not reopen or independently
decode the MES source. This preserves the closed GDScript Phase 1-4 record
ownership boundary.

Every typed instruction becomes one source-qualified statement node. Its
operands retain the complete expression AST and any additional low-level
metadata. Every strict-analysis opaque tail becomes one explicit opaque node
with `byte_preserving_fail_closed` evidence; it cannot acquire an opcode,
dialogue, or guessed semantic label. All nodes retain source entry, region,
code-relative `[start,end)`, raw bytes and SHA-256, zero or more partial-CFG
node coordinates, and every contained message/code/state/resource reference.
A node may have no CFG coordinate because the handoff graph is intentionally
bounded; the empty list is evidence of no supplied graph node, not an inferred
fallthrough.

The v1 linear source form stores the exact pre-code container bytes separately
from ordered statement/opaque bytes. Validation requires bootstrap and
address-table regions, nodes, and reference ownership to form exact partitions;
`preamble + ordered node bytes` must reproduce both the original entry SHA-256
and bytecode SHA-256. The output has its own canonical JSON fingerprint and
retains the input handoff fingerprint and exact component-schema lock.

The focused authoritative `D_TALK00.MES` handoff lifts code-relative
`0x0000..0xF70D` into 9,266 typed nodes with no opaque node and deterministic
payload fingerprint `d3b30a2f...ac9728e`. Its supplied CFG remains anchored at
the previously audited owning range `0x07C9..0x084A`; nodes outside that bounded
graph retain empty CFG links. The separate authoritative `08C.MES` handoff
lifts all 25,021 code bytes into 3,103 typed nodes plus the exact 57-byte opaque
node at address-table `entry_0032`, `0x0E62..0x0E9B`, with payload fingerprint
`4dc7ef16...9f556ff`. The source archive was unchanged during handoff creation.

Evidence type: current GDScript handoff validation against the authoritative
archive, Python schema/fingerprint validation without source reparsing, exact
container reversal, deterministic repeated lifting, and synthetic mutation,
gap, CFG-map, reference-map, expression, metadata, and opaque-boundary tests.
Confidence is **Confirmed** for the linear IR schema, byte ownership, source
reversal, and handoff provenance. It remains **Unresolved** for the native or
gameplay meaning of opaque bytes, numeric slots and selectors, and any control
structure not yet proven in MD-02.
