## Phase 6 Editable IR and No-Op Compiler Baseline

Content Core `0.230.0` reserves `kakyu_mes_editable_ir/v1` and
`kakyu_mes_noop_compile_audit/v1`. The editable document embeds one complete,
fingerprinted `kakyu_mes_decompiler_ir/v1` as its immutable source and carries
an ordered `operations` array. V1 currently advertises no supported operation:
the array must be empty, unknown fields and operations are rejected even after
rehashing, opaque-record policy is source-byte preservation, and relocation is
explicitly not performed. This freezes a safe authoring input boundary without
pretending that variable-length edits already compile.

`tools/compile_mes_noop.py` reconstructs the source preamble followed by every
ordered typed or opaque node byte, independently reopens the MES header and
strictly increasing address table, and emits a new binary plus compact audit.
The compiler requires distinct, previously absent output paths. It verifies a
temporary before exclusive publication, publishes the audit last, and removes
its newly published binary if audit publication fails. The audit binds source,
editable-IR, and decompiler fingerprints; container/bytecode/preamble hashes;
region/node/opaque coverage; zero edit and relocation counts; and exact
byte-identity invariants.

The first authoritative check consumes source-bound `01M.MES` over the full
code-relative range `0x0000..0x15DA6`. Its 426-entry, 91,218-byte output is
byte-identical at entry SHA-256
`a50511b0ad0ad446b7988c3cfb36736424bf6617e9eb952e20b505f745607cc5`
and bytecode SHA-256
`f590b3007ea98dcce6f10bc85eb316abdf250f6417a87cec4ab0a6d98ed2230b`.
All 11,537 nodes are retained; this entry has no opaque node, while the
synthetic regression separately requires an opaque tail to survive exactly.
The editable document fingerprint is
`3d7c8ef577e8571cb6dd42bbaf0442ba363d0b7f7e9dd32332ce0e666fe1b7f0`
and the compile-audit fingerprint is
`e831def0256787a24c8d778b4193530c7b142715033ddbebabd81a08f899c5e2`.
The source archive remains unchanged. Evidence type: authoritative source-bound
Phase 1-4 handoff, validated Phase 5 JSON, exact binary comparison, independent
Python container reopen, and synthetic typed/opaque mutation regressions.
Confidence is **Confirmed** for the Python zero-operation compiler boundary.
Content Core `0.231.0` additionally reserves
`kakyu_mes_noop_reopen_audit/v1`. The GDScript consumer validates the exact

It then independently parses the emitted MES with `KakyuMesContainer`, rebuilds

`be77152c116921355e37ea99e4c71e7c5e7dbc6c814bfcb156e82e01bef5f947`
and reopen-audit fingerprint
`27cd1c61c94f29945273ca5cf02941a63776b81078288a3f0bb92fd85a1f55c6`.
Evidence type: the same source-bound Phase 5 handoff and Python no-op audit,

### Phase 6 Variable-Length Message Relocation Preflight

owner, strict CP932 source and replacement bytes, an unchanged native
double-byte projection, and a variable byte length. The output is deterministic

The plan retains the exact source instruction and payload bounds, replacement
node bytes, byte delta, output code size, every changed address-table cell,
counts of following nodes and regions, and old/new source and target
coordinates for affected references. A shifted opaque node is an explicit
blocker. An encoded code target whose numeric operand must change is also a
blocker owned by MW-03; derived conditional fallthrough coordinates do not
invent an encoded patch. `assembly_ready` is true only when no blocker remains.

`8c0e519f8999545945c9186423049de5fe01078a4d769fba45e02f609c776256`.

### Phase 6 Branch and Continuation Target-Repair Plan

Content Core `0.237.0` reserves
`kakyu_mes_control_target_relocation_plan/v1`. The Python planner consumes the
unchanged editable IR plus an exact `kakyu_mes_message_relocation_plan/v1`; it
does not replace or broaden the frozen MW-02 contract. It examines only
`encoded_code_target_requires_mw03` blockers. Every other blocker is copied to
`remaining_blockers`, so `assembly_ready` remains false until all independent
boundaries are safe.

V1 supports two encoded forms. A typed command `0x0B`
`branch_if_not_true` must retain its validated condition expression over the
bytes immediately after the command, and its last four instruction bytes are
the absolute code-relative false target in little-endian `u32` form. A typed
command `0x0C` `continuation_transfer` must be exactly five bytes, with its
four-byte target beginning one byte after the command. In both cases the
indexed reference kind and operand value must agree with those bytes, and the
old target must be an in-code, aligned, unique typed instruction start. The
plan records exact source and output instruction/operand `[start,end)` ranges,
old and new target coordinates, old and new four-byte encodings, and the
owning and target node identities. Overlapping output patches, unresolved or
non-instruction targets, stale bytes, and unsupported transfer forms remain
fail-closed. This unit publishes JSON only; applying the patches and claiming
an assembled output remain open within MW-03.

The source-bound audit uses authoritative `mes.arc` entry `03C.MES`, whose
entry SHA-256 is
`79d355a0b9c8025a419647d293ed8b908f45a81ff43ba183a326921d097d62d2`.
The continuation at code-relative `0x3EF0..0x3EF5` stores its target in
`0x3EF1..0x3EF5`; the retained value `0x3FA9` is an aligned typed
`global_u8_write_run` at `0x3FA9..0x3FAF`. A two-byte expansion of the typed
message at `0x3EFF..0x3F03` therefore leaves the earlier operand position
unchanged and plans its target as `0x3FAB`. The resulting Python plan has one
resolved continuation patch, no remaining blocker, and fingerprint
`8bbf8ead9d855d7b3b91b0f840195803c1fcb6f1c5c9a7836cb84f5c96017ac9`;
the independent Godot validator accepts the transported JSON with
`mes_bytes=false`.

The same entry supplies a variable-condition branch sample at
`0x02A6..0x02B1`: its validated expression occupies `0x02A7..0x02AD`, the
target operand occupies the trailing `0x02AD..0x02B1`, and target `0x0C8F` is
an aligned typed instruction start. A separate two-byte message expansion at
`0x02B6..0x02E8` requires 71 encoded repairs: 52 conditional false targets and
19 continuations. The planner resolves all 71 with no remaining blocker; Godot
accepts the transported plan with fingerprint
`f9ef49dce3130bd0d0726b79e1c1043d0c000967b420cb3be58df7a58ac043ca`.
Evidence type: direct read-only
authoritative ARC entry, exact Phase 1-5 source projection, deterministic
Python planning, synthetic branch/continuation regressions, and independent
Godot 4.7 JSON validation. Confidence is **Confirmed** for these structural
operand encodings and fail-closed planning rules. No new native pixel, cadence,
control-effect, or original-engine edited-output claim is made. The archive
remained at SHA-256
`31a95b31cb0f1051cf973a4dba4f4a5405671e4488240adfafb9b02290986aa6`.

An MES address-table cell is also a sorted region boundary, not merely an

code offset by four, and reports the exact nodes and references that would move
to the new region. The bytecode, all code-relative coordinates, and every
encoded code target remain unchanged. The output is JSON only; it neither
publishes an MES container nor claims that a native host selects the added
entry.

### Phase 6 Control-Body Insertion and Removal Plan

Content Core `0.258.0` reserves
`kakyu_mes_control_body_edit_plan/v1` for the final planning boundary of
MW-06. It accepts either one contiguous strict-typed donor span copied before
an exact typed anchor in the same address-table entry, or one contiguous
strict-typed span removed strictly inside an entry. The donor must precede its
anchor. The plan binds the source bytes and per-node hashes, every shifted
address cell and region, every affected source-map node and reference, every
encoded command-`0x0B`, command-`0x0C`, and command-`0x10` target repair, and
every changed CFG node/edge identifier. It publishes JSON only.

V1 deliberately fails closed rather than guessing ownership. A donor or
removed node that owns a reference or CFG node is blocked, as is an implicit
command-`0x10` target in the body. An incoming code target or CFG node exactly
at an insertion anchor is blocked because choosing whether it should enter the
new body or the relocated original anchor is a semantic edit. Removal is
blocked when a reference source or code target lies inside the deleted span.
Any shifted opaque node is blocked. Any supplied call/resume or trace evidence
also blocks V1 assembly until a later contract can relocate that evidence
exactly. These are valid diagnostic plans with `assembly_ready=false`, not
partially authorized edits.

(entry SHA-256
`79d355a0b9c8025a419647d293ed8b908f45a81ff43ba183a326921d097d62d2`).

trace evidence and has no opaque node.

diff does not trust a compiler-produced list of changed bytes alone. It
independently reconstructs the intended output body edit, target operands, and
address-table cells, requires byte identity with the reopened output, and
lifts the output handoff through the same Phase 5 linear IR boundary.

Every source node is classified exactly once as retained or removed. Every
output node is accounted for exactly once as retained or inserted. Retained
nodes are mapped by relocated `[start,end)` coordinates; their raw bytes must
remain identical except for the target operands explicitly listed in the
compile audit. Each listed non-definition target must also rebuild as one
aligned in-code reference at its output coordinate. Opaque nodes have a
stronger invariant: source and output counts must match and every source
opaque node must map once with identical raw bytes. A synthetic regression
retains one unrelated opaque node across both insertion and removal and
rejects rehashed reference, unrelated-byte, node-count, and opaque-accounting
mutations. The JSON contract is independently fingerprinted and validated in

### Proof-Bounded Control Transfers

Content Core `0.204.0` reserves `kakyu_mes_control_flow_proof/v1` for the first
MD-02 projection. `tools/prove_mes_control_flow.py` accepts only a validated
linear decompiler IR. A `branch_if_not_true` becomes a proved conditional only
when it owns exactly one confirmed true-fallthrough edge and one confirmed
false-target edge, the retained condition has an AST, the true target equals
the source instruction end, and the false target equals the retained
code-offset operand. A `continuation_transfer` likewise requires exactly one
confirmed edge whose target equals its operand.

Every graph edge is owned by exactly one output construct. Unsupported edge
shapes and operand/graph disagreements become explicit `unresolved_transfer`
constructs instead of guessed control flow. A transfer opcode introduced only
as the terminal node of the bounded graph has no supplied outgoing edge; it is
an `unexpanded_transfer_anchor`, distinct from malformed or missing edge data.
Opaque or decode-stop graph nodes remain `boundary_anchor` constructs. These
rules intentionally prove transfers, not yet reducible `if` bodies, joins,
loops, dispatch tables, or call/return regions.

non-transfer graph nodes remain ordinary anchors, while four conditional leaves
and one continuation leaf at expansion depth remain explicit unexpanded
anchors. The deterministic proof fingerprint is
`e08a8d75...c8a2f252`. The `08C.MES` opaque graph has no transfer edge and
retains its one `0x0E62..0x0E9B` boundary anchor; its proof fingerprint is
`282e847b...2b419ca`.

Evidence type: schema-validated linear IR derived from the current authoritative

deterministic repeated projection, and synthetic confirmed, changed-target,

- an ordinary typed instruction with no unresolved control transfer;
- a character-stream dispatch token whose handler family, consumption rule,
  probe start/end/count, NUL stop, raw payload bytes, and exact stored-order
  node partition all agree; or
- a literal command-`0x1D` node with a matching source-bound return
  certificate whose physical resume is that node's exact end.

The proof does not rewrite Phase 2 record boundaries. Stored-order rows inside
a native character payload remain in the lossless linear IR and are listed as
payload node IDs beneath their execution owner. Opaque nodes, non-NUL probe
stops, changed raw bytes, incomplete partitions, command-`0x00`, branch or
continuation transfers, and unproved shared calls reject the whole anchor
span.

V2 separately maps every certified literal call node to the exact same-region
linear node beginning at its physical resume. This is a source-qualified
linear-CFG overlay: it neither invents a target label nor removes the original
numeric call statement. Missing, duplicate, cross-region, or shape-mismatched
resume coordinates are rejected, and unresolved call certificates are copied
as fallback edge rejections.

On the unchanged authoritative `GROUND.MES` entry, the focused proof has four
anchor candidates: two proved and two rejected. The significant proved edge
is `L_000016EB -> L_0000170F`, covering source range `0x16F0..0x170F` and
eleven exact linear nodes. Its retained execution segments are:

- ordinary source marker `0x16F0..0x16F5`;
- character-stream owner `0x16F5` plus NUL-terminated payload
  `0x16F6..0x16FA` (payload SHA-256
  `1fa44a9118e2025e23deb021ba059ad7f2bf6b1ed96c195186d7e838f19cf8e6`);
- character-stream owner `0x16FA` plus its one-byte NUL payload
  `0x16FB..0x16FC` (payload SHA-256
  `6e340b9cffb37a989ca544e6bb780a2c78901d3fb33738768511a30617afa01d`);
- the certified routine-3 call `0x16FC..0x1701`; and
- ordinary typed records `0x1701..0x170F`.

All 441 certified GROUND calls have one exact same-region resume node and emit
441 call-return edges. The 39 cyclic-callee fallbacks emit no edge and retain
their shared-call rejection reason. The proof fingerprint is
`34bb8cbce26ebe205d62c8dc89c7039e476a3465d5eccc464e78b597aec057f1`.
Evidence type: unchanged authoritative archive handoff, the EXE-confirmed
single-byte presentation consumption contract already recorded above, exact
raw-byte and node-partition checks, regenerated shared-call certificate, and
synthetic missing-call, missing-resume, changed-terminator, and mutation
regressions.
Confidence is **Confirmed** for this numeric same-region fallthrough.
Natural-loop v2 consumes the edge while retaining the full fallback;
presentation pixels and cursor effects remain outside this structural proof.

complete semantic name. `LIBLARY.LIB` requires targeted scanners because it
has no normal address table and is excluded from normal-script coverage.

## Analysis Rules

- Keep numeric stores and offsets when their names are not proven.
- Distinguish an event's internal branch from the caller condition that makes
  the event available.
- Confirm cross-script flow at the caller, not only by finding a filename in a
  callee.
- Preserve decode diagnostics and fail closed when an expression is invalid.
- Regenerate ignored IR when needed; do not commit lossless bytecode or text
  projections as documentation.

## Phase 6 same-width state-literal edit plan

`kakyu_mes_state_literal_edit_plan/v1` is the first bounded MW-04 authoring
contract. It consumes the immutable editable/decompiler JSON rather than
reparsing a container, selects one typed write instruction by code-relative
start plus exact instruction SHA-256, and selects one expression/continuation
pair by index. A valid source expression must be exactly one canonical literal:
an unambiguous one-byte `0x00..0x7F` token, an `0xF1` 16-bit literal, or an
`0xF2` 32-bit literal, each with its expression terminator. The replacement
keeps the same width and byte length. Destination storage/index expression,
bank, pair count, continuation byte, record boundary, and every byte outside
the expression are retained. V1 emits JSON only; changed MES assembly and
native-engine execution remain separate gates.

The source-bound audit re-read authoritative `mes.arc` entry `03C.MES`
(entry SHA-256
`79d355a0b9c8025a419647d293ed8b908f45a81ff43ba183a326921d097d62d2`)
and selected the typed `global_u8_write_run` at `0x3FA9..0x3FAF`. Its numeric
destination is storage `global_u8`, bank 0, index 286. Pair 0 is the exact
8-bit literal expression at `0x3FAC..0x3FAE`, followed by the unchanged zero
continuation byte at `0x3FAE`. Planning the numeric value `1 -> 0` produced
plan fingerprint
`39892e4773f13ae74c5cb78f54e9a08194df47571feec7acfce8863fc8bdd6a6`;
the source archive SHA-256 remained
`31a95b31cb0f1051cf973a4dba4f4a5405671e4488240adfafb9b02290986aa6`.
Evidence type: unchanged authoritative archive handoff, exact Phase 1-5 typed
node/source bytes, and deterministic Python plan validation. Confidence is
**Confirmed** for the record, literal, and continuation boundaries and for the
numeric storage coordinate. The gameplay meaning of slot 286 and original
runtime behavior after modification are unresolved and are not claimed.
Godot 4.7 independently accepted the same source-bound plan and fingerprint
through Content Core `0.239.0`; its validator also rejects non-integral JSON
coordinates, typed-command/destination mismatches, ambiguous 8-bit tokens,
changed continuation bytes, and patches outside the selected expression.

The bounded Python assembler consumed that exact plan and exclusively
published a 16,949-byte disposable `03C.MES` output plus compile audit. The

`594db610852c7748745389dfbf95a6f64dc064d60ab4bf224222066e11c4e572`.
An exhaustive byte comparison found exactly one changed container byte, at

The changed entry SHA-256 is
`be0615b90fb3798b4d687fd6f4f2525f15885971bcfe4b9b7fc68e6c22c96ed4`
and compile-audit fingerprint is
`6065d9e8d5c4c6af95619976a6a7dd536f356ad09c11c7f5a03b57c8e607ec0c`.

## Phase 6 same-width condition-literal edit plan

`kakyu_mes_condition_literal_edit_plan/v1` is the bounded MW-04 condition
authoring preflight. It consumes the immutable editable/decompiler JSON,
selects one typed `branch_if_not_true` command (`0x0B`) by code-relative start
and exact instruction SHA-256, then selects one literal AST leaf by its exact
source offset. A valid literal is one canonical unambiguous `0x00..0x7F`
8-bit token, `0xF1` plus a 16-bit value, or `0xF2` plus a 32-bit value. The
replacement must retain that width and byte length. The contract separately
binds the expression's final `0xFF`, the unique indexed
`condition_false_target` reference, and the trailing four-byte little-endian
target operand. Consequently a selected literal cannot absorb the expression
terminator or rewrite the branch target as an incidental payload. V1 emits
JSON only; assembly, changed-container reopen, and original-engine execution
remain separate gates.

terminator remains at `0x013A`. The retained false-target operand occupies

`4cc508a256ca3a02925eef3ec8d11c6c7a2ab846f38169f36528518a35b266bf`.
The authoritative archive SHA-256 remains
`31a95b31cb0f1051cf973a4dba4f4a5405671e4488240adfafb9b02290986aa6`.

instruction/AST/reference bytes, and deterministic Python plan validation.

## Phase 6 same-length resource-name edit plan

`kakyu_mes_resource_name_edit_plan/v1` is the bounded MW-04 resource preflight.
It consumes the immutable editable/decompiler JSON and accepts only one resource
reference that is both owned by the selected typed instruction and indexed with
boundary `strict_indexed`. V1 supports the already bounded
`mmo_resource_marker`, `ax_resource_marker`, and `voice_marker` records. Inline
MES/LIB execution names are deliberately excluded because changing a called
script belongs to the MW-05 nested-call contract.

The operation binds the code-relative instruction start, exact instruction
SHA-256, and decompiler resource-reference ID. Both source and replacement must
be printable-ASCII safe entry names, keep the resource form's extension, and
have the same encoded length. The plan separately hashes the bytes before the
name, the name, and the bytes after it. The fixed marker selector/envelope and
all numeric operands therefore remain byte-identical, including numeric fields
whose native meaning is not part of this authoring contract. V1 emits JSON only;
it does not prove that a replacement entry exists, publish a changed MES, or
claim original-engine compatibility.

`kakyu_mes_inline_script_name_edit_plan/v1` opens the first bounded MW-05
nested-call authoring subgate. It consumes the immutable editable/decompiler
JSON and accepts exactly one indexed `inline_script_execution` reference. The
record must retain presentation subcommand 8, selector 2 with a `.LIB` name or
selector 3 with a `.MES` name, the corresponding library/definition-bootstrap
role, confirmed native context restore, and tool-side non-execution policy.
Both names must be safe printable ASCII, retain the selector-specific
extension, and have the same byte length.

The selected envelope may be a strict typed instruction or an already indexed

operation binds that owner's full raw SHA-256, the envelope coordinate, and the
decompiler reference ID. The plan separately hashes the fixed seven-byte
selector prefix, name bytes, two-NUL suffix, and complete envelope; every owner
byte outside the name remains frozen. V1 publishes JSON only. It neither checks
that the replacement archive entry exists nor claims that a modified container

## Phase 6 registered-definition registry proof

Content Core `0.247.0` reserves
`kakyu_mes_registered_definition_registry_proof/v1` as the source-bound body
binding required before command-`0x11` invocation editing. The Python analyzer
reads one original MES entry directly, follows its instruction-aligned
zero-start path, and accepts only command-`0x14` registrations with one
unambiguous 8-bit literal selector. Each proof row binds the complete
registration instruction, selector and expression coordinates, and the exact
unexecuted `[instruction_end, skip_target)` body bytes. The path must be
acyclic, retain only the already bounded registration/fallthrough commands,
and reach command-`0x00`. Command-`0x10` is explicitly classified as the
separate choice-definition-body family and cannot enter this registry proof.

The unchanged authoritative `mes.arc` supplies `DEF_MAIN.MES` (entry SHA-256
`f2012ce5d90f60a5d1ca8190e03571341c0384c2d3d96e9aec2b3ab949db0ef0`).
The 5,444-byte container has one address-table cell, code offset 8, and 5,436
code bytes. Its zero-start path contains 42 instructions and reaches the return
at `0x153B`, registering 14 unique selectors in stored execution order:
18, 81, 26, 11, 12, 14, 15, 17, 21, 22, 23, 20, 80, and 99. In particular,
selector 11 is registered at `0x042D..0x0434` with body
`0x0434..0x049A`; selector 14 is registered at `0x0EFB..0x0F02` with body
`0x0F02..0x0F4B`. The proof fingerprint is
`eddaf97cd1b5fd5c88ebd259e2aebc82a203b1d79abde2467e625a25dc2ff0e2`.

Evidence type: direct read-only authoritative archive decode, exact container,
instruction and body hashes, deterministic zero-start structural traversal,
and independent current-GDScript startup-context audit of the same 14 selector
and body boundaries. Confidence is **Confirmed** for the command-`0x14`
registration order and exact body ranges. Body execution effects, registration
lifetime outside the audited startup path, and native compatibility of any
future changed command-`0x11` call remain **Unresolved**.

`kakyu_mes_registered_definition_call_edit_plan/v1` consumes that frozen
registry proof together with the existing editable IR and call-family proof.
It accepts one typed command-`0x11` call containing exactly one expression
record whose selector is an unambiguous 8-bit literal. The plan binds the full
five-byte call, literal and terminators, unique physical resume node, and the
complete source and replacement registry rows. It deliberately emits no MES
bytes and no return edge: exact registered-body bounds do not by themselves

The authoritative `01M.MES` entry (entry SHA-256
`a50511b0ad0ad446b7988c3cfb36736424bf6617e9eb952e20b505f745607cc5`)

`b9e1b30a80cf55ff6e853fabc0b798e7d2ad6ac31a683085e9ac483bf6f1fae6`.

## Effect Record Boundary Correction (Instruction v45)

Content Core `0.275.0` consumes presentation subcommand 6 as one complete
typed-record list, rather than a leading control byte followed by shadow
banked writes. Authoritative `LIBLARY.LIB` routine 9 supplies the bounded
examples: selector-1 stop at `0x0EAD..0x0EB9`, selector-0 named load at
`0x10D9..0x10F3` and `0x1103..0x111D`. The original presentation dispatcher
routes subcommand 6 through `0x0042823C` to adapter `0x00429D70` and handler
`0x00429E00`, using typed-list parser `0x0043E800`. See [Audio](audio.md)
for the archive, filename, native restart and source-call evidence.

Instruction v45 emits `effect_request` only for the exact three-record
shape: literal selector 0, a safe ASCII WAV entry name, and a valid channel
expression. Every other complete list remains an `effect_dispatch` with
preserved records and unresolved execution semantics; malformed/truncated
lists fail closed at the outer command without exposing their payload.
Event trace v68 emits a non-executing `effect_request` with the resource,
channel and exact source range, or `effect_dispatch_omitted`. No audio device
or native stop is invoked by the analyzer. These are metadata, not gameplay
writes; generic argument/state aliasing is not implicitly introduced.
Old v44 handoffs must be regenerated, not silently consumed by Python.

The older native-presentation v3 interpretation of EVENTB03's seven literal
subcommand-12 records above described only the generic character-stream
fallback. The newer source-qualified dispatcher audit reaches native wait
adapter `0x0042B040` and loop `0x0042B070` for this route. Values 20/40 become
counter thresholds 6/13, not glyph identities. The effect consumer projects
these onto a nominal 15-ms tool clock; early native input interruption and
host wall-clock equivalence remain unresolved. This refinement does not
authorize executing unknown character-stream payloads.

Evidence type: direct read-only authoritative MES/LIB and SE ARC inspection,
original embedded-runtime dispatch/handler checks, strict/structural GDScript
parity, and deterministic tests. Confidence: **Confirmed** for record extent,
bounded named-effect routing and native counter calculation; **Unresolved**
for arbitrary selectors, generalized runtime alias ownership and exact device
cadence. Reproduce with `tools/audit_eventb03_sound.py`.

The v45 read-only alignment pass covers all 1,016 entries and 18,079,488 code
bytes: 363,850 compound records include 191 subcommand-6 envelopes across 46
entries; the sole structural opaque tail remains the 57 bytes in `08C.MES`.
The strict analysis pass retains 1,180 byte-preserving opaque boundaries and
220,493 message rows, all with typed owners and zero native/expression/opaque
payload conflicts. These aligned counts do not claim that every raw byte
prefix is an executable entrypoint or that all native effects are implemented.

## Logical Expressions Use Exact-One Truth (Core 0.276.0)

The [EVENTB03 face-flag audit](eventb03_face_flag_routes.md) prompted an
independent check of native expression tokens `0xE6` (`logical_and`) and
`0xE7` (`logical_or`). Both test **equality to the numeric value 1**, not
generic nonzero truth. Both operands are evaluated before the operator;
neither token introduces short-circuit execution.

The authoritative source configuration and original executable were reread.
Input SHA-256 is
`3fef4e2f6dde28c8aaa754a01accca4acadedb0dc67b25d298a303ad350a82f5`;
the embedded runtime at file offset `0x1B000` has SHA-256
`5b49d5e2162b07420aaa1c9298677150e0a33d9c84ee8be09f1c719aad8597da`.
The separate `tools/audit_mes_logical_truth.py` retains the existing full
native audit v317 identity check and adds bounded dispatch, call, comparison,
branch, literal-result and handler-span checks. v317 alone did not cover
these two handler windows. The original program is not executed or patched.

Dispatch at `0x00405F84..0x00405F9E` subtracts `0x80` from the token and
uses byte map `0x0040669C` followed by jump table `0x00406628`. E6 and E7
map at `0x00406702/0x00406703` to slots 9/10; their table cells at
`0x0040664C/0x00406650` target the respective handlers below. The standalone
auditor verifies those mappings rather than inferring operators from nearby
machine instructions alone.

| Token | Native virtual-address interval | Confirmed result rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E6 | `0x0040629D..0x004062DC` | 1 iff left == 1 and right == 1, else 0 |
| E7 | `0x004062DC..0x00406321` | 1 iff left == 1 or right == 1, else 0 |

The E6 handler's 63-byte span hash is
`2b5b9215d92137ef716120842d2163fd9c2615b6cc738c226247c5c5b8e5a466`.
Both operands are popped at calls `0x0040629F` and `0x004062A8`; the second
pop is compared with 1 at `0x004062AD`, then the retained first pop is
compared with that value at `0x004062B2`. Either failed comparison goes to
the zero-result path at `0x004062C8`.

The E7 handler's 69-byte span hash is
`d35825e438cabdf63977033da221648ee324d7fc278fc51a782f904dc5e7d3d8`.
After both pops, comparisons at `0x004062EC` and `0x004062F1` independently
test equality to 1. Either equality reaches the literal-one path at
`0x0040630A`; otherwise `0x004062F6` produces zero. The common command-0x0B
branch already requires an evaluated result equal to 1 at native
`0x004190F5`, matching the existing Event Runner rule.

These deliberately synthetic examples distinguish the correction:

| Input expression | Native result | Former generic-nonzero result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `logical_and(2, 1)` | 0 | 1 |
| `logical_or(0, 2)` | 0 | 1 |
| `logical_and(not_equal(2, 0), 1)` | 1 | 1 |

Core 0.276.0 changes only the two logical-operation predicates in
`mes_expression.gd`; the persistent-stack evaluator delegates to the same
implementation. The bounded Python PROMIS location-predicate evaluator now
uses the same exact-one AND rule. Numeric flag values must not be normalized
implicitly. Bitwise E8/E9 remain numeric operations, and explicit comparison
nodes still return 0/1. The expression tests first reproduced the two
counterexamples against the old implementation, then checked all ordered
pairs of `0,1,2,255,65535,0xFFFFFFFF` in both literal and state forms,
nested logic, explicit comparisons, bitwise results, persistent-stack
evaluation, input preservation and eager RNG operand evaluation.

The source-checked `B_PIC.MES:0x0568..0x0597` guard supplies a useful
unaffected original case: each logical child is a comparison or another
normalized logical result. Its 72 zero-entry EVENTB03 traces remain fixed by
the linked audit. This correction does not authorize any nonzero-flag product
preset or assign gameplay names to those numeric flags.

Instruction v45 and trace v68 shapes, record extents and the language-neutral
AST remain unchanged. Previously cached **execution results** involving raw
nonboolean E6/E7 operands must be recomputed; changing a version label is not
revalidation. This unit does not claim a new whole-corpus execution proof or
general native arithmetic-width, overflow, RNG-algorithm or pixel equivalence.

Evidence type: direct original-EXE static control/data-flow checks, exact
handler hashes, current-Core read-only original MES replay, and independent
synthetic regressions. Confidence: **Confirmed** for the stated E6/E7
exact-one/eager semantics; unrelated numeric operations and native effects
remain outside this bounded correction.

Validation for this correction: the native supplemental audit passed 42
checks and its synthetic/mutation suite passed 9 tests; the bounded Python
location predicate, validation runner and boolean-DNF suites passed 7, 7
and 5 tests respectively. All 57 MES test scenes exited successfully,
including 325 expression checks and 146 Event Runner checks. Event Player
and Catalog passed 996 and 73 checks. Original B03 state12/affection/face-flag
audits retained 139/339/1,161 checks, and the source-backed B03, B14 and D02
presentation/terminal regressions passed with their source archives unchanged.
The project parse passed. No additional user-controlled UI verification was
requested or inferred from these automated results.

## State reference index completes the write runs (Core 0.320.0)

MA-11, found 2026-09-10 while measuring the 01M caller group:
`references.state` carried a `write` row for a `global_u8_write_run` and for
the banked u16/i32 runs, but none for a `state_u16_write_run`
(`EVENTG11.MES:250..255`, `state_u16[8] <- 0`), and for a run whose value is
an expression only the read operands (`01M.MES:43109..43120`, `state_u16[5] <-
banked_u16[2] & 128`). The destination was always in the instruction's index
operand, so the typed IR was complete and the reference index was not; the
analysis inventory's `write_sites` inherited the gap, which is why two dead
route inputs were found only by runtime tracing.

Core 0.320.0 (2026-09-15) gives every write run whose destination is a state
storage its write row, in both producers (`content_core/mes_analysis_index.gd`
and `tools/mes_references.py`, checked against each other by the Godot oracle
test): `0x04` (`state_u16`, the u8 index as a decimal string), `0x05` (a
dynamic `global_u8`, the destination expression summarised as its literal or
`expression`, the way the banked runs already were; the command keeps its
older flat operand shape, one pair operand per pair), `0x06` (`banked_u8`,
with its bank) and `0x0A` (`global_i32`). The two argument-slot runs (`0x09`,
`0x16`) carry no write row: the index emits no write row for argument-slot runs;
their storage is `global_i32`, which the runner models since 0.377.0 (above), and
extending the index to a `0x09` write row is deferred (it would move the frozen
v45 digest). Row order is unchanged:
the write row first, then the operand reads in preorder, including the reads
inside an expression destination or value.

The frozen instruction-v45 digest was regenerated: 667 of 1,016 payloads
changed, all of them in the `references` component only (667 reference
digests; container, record alignment, typed IR and capability report are
byte-identical), the state-reference count grew from 540,539 to 561,522, and
the corpus fingerprint moved from `617111b9...d94277b` to
`74f1408836440b7194ffb25aaa498aa8b61bda695326ed148ccd35a562a1dff8`;
`tools/audit_mes_handoff_equivalence.py --require-full-equivalent` reproduces
it from Python over all 1,016 entries. The owner approved the new
fingerprint on 2026-09-15 (`todo/mes_analyzer.md`, "Current Verification
Gate"). No record boundary changed.
